st.up.accused_holds_the_hot_axe.l: What is most real in you is unseen, everywhere, and the same in all.
st.up.accused_holds_the_hot_axe.s: Uddalaka teaches his son through everyday experiments: a fast that dims the mind, a bird on a string, rivers merging in the sea, a banyan seed with nothing visible inside, salt dissolved in water, a blindfolded man finding his way home. Each lesson ends: 'That subtle essence is the self of all. You are that, Shvetaketu.'

st.up.artabhaga_take_my_hand.l: Ask your hard questions bravely, and give credit where it is due.
st.up.artabhaga_take_my_hand.s: King Janaka offers a thousand cows to the wisest scholar. Yajnavalkya claims them and is challenged by one learned man after another. Gargi, the only woman, rises twice like a warrior with two arrows, then graciously tells the hall none of them can beat him. Yajnavalkya closes by asking what root a person grows from when cut down by death.
st.up.artabhaga_take_my_hand.t: Gargi questions Yajnavalkya at Janaka's court

st.up.bhrigu_sent_back.l: A wise parent lets a child discover the answer instead of handing it over.
st.up.bhrigu_sent_back.s: Bhrigu asks his father Varuna to teach him what is ultimate. Varuna gives only a clue and tells him to reflect. Bhrigu comes back four times with answers (food, breath, mind, understanding) and each time is sent back to go deeper, until he discovers that everything is born from joy, lives by joy and returns to joy.

st.up.brihadratha_frog_in_dry_well.l: Even success can leave you feeling stuck; asking for help is the first step out.
st.up.brihadratha_frog_in_dry_well.s: A king hands his throne to his son and goes to the forest, overwhelmed by how everything decays. When a sage offers him a wish, he says he feels like a frog in a dark well and asks to be shown the way out.

st.up.chariot.l: Hold the reins of your mind, or your senses will drive for you.
st.up.chariot.s: Yama pictures a person as a chariot: the self is the rider, the body the chariot, the intellect the driver, the mind the reins and the senses the horses. With a steady mind the horses obey; without it they bolt. He ends with the call to arise and wake.

st.up.convocation_parting_words.l: Truth, right action, gratitude and graceful giving: a whole life in one speech.
st.up.convocation_parting_words.s: As a student finishes his studies and leaves to start family life, the teacher gives him parting instructions: speak truth, do right, keep learning, honour mother, father, teacher and guest, give with grace. He even tells the student to copy only the teachers' good conduct, and when in doubt to act as thoughtful, gentle people would.

st.up.da_da_da.l: Each of us hears the lesson we most need: restraint, generosity or compassion.
st.up.da_da_da.s: Gods, humans and demons finish their studies with their father Prajapati and ask for a parting word. To each he says only 'Da'. The gods hear 'be self-controlled', humans hear 'give', and demons hear 'be compassionate'. The thunder still repeats it.
st.up.da_da_da.t: Da Da Da: the voice of thunder

st.up.family_around_the_dying.l: What is most real in you is unseen, everywhere, and the same in all.
st.up.family_around_the_dying.s: Uddalaka teaches his son through everyday experiments: a fast that dims the mind, a bird on a string, rivers merging in the sea, a banyan seed with nothing visible inside, salt dissolved in water, a blindfolded man finding his way home. Each lesson ends: 'That subtle essence is the self of all. You are that, Shvetaketu.'
st.up.family_around_the_dying.who: the relatives of the dying man

st.up.father_and_son_back_to_school.l: A parent who says 'let's learn together' teaches more than any answer.
st.up.father_and_son_back_to_school.s: A patron asks young Shvetaketu a question he cannot answer. He asks his father, who admits he does not know either and suggests they both go to the patron as students. Chitra welcomes Uddalaka for his humility.
st.up.father_and_son_back_to_school.t: Father and son go back to school

st.up.fathers_last_handing_over.l: Parents pass on far more than property; they pass on themselves.
st.up.fathers_last_handing_over.s: When a father feels death near, he lies down and his son lies over him, and they exchange words: the father places his speech, breath, sight, hearing, joys and sorrows in the son, and the son receives each one.

st.up.first_being_afraid_alone.l: Fear and loneliness are human; truth gives even the weak a footing.
st.up.first_being_afraid_alone.s: In this creation story the first being, alone, feels fear, then realises there is no one else to fear. He feels no joy alone and longs for a companion, splitting into husband and wife. Finally dharma is created, the truth by which even the weak can stand up to the strong.
st.up.first_being_afraid_alone.t: The first being: fear, loneliness and dharma

st.up.five_householders_ashvapati.l: Point people to someone who knows more, and say plainly what you came for.
st.up.five_householders_ashvapati.s: Five great scholars come to Uddalaka to learn. Knowing he cannot answer everything, he takes them to King Ashvapati instead. The king proudly says his kingdom has no thieves or drunkards and offers gifts, but the scholars politely insist on the purpose they came for.
st.up.five_householders_ashvapati.t: Five scholars go to King Ashvapati

st.up.indra_virochana.l: Don't settle for the first comfortable answer; keep asking until it holds.
st.up.indra_virochana.s: Indra of the gods and Virochana of the demons study with Prajapati for 32 years to learn the self. Shown their dressed-up reflections, both leave satisfied; Virochana goes home teaching that the body is everything. Indra stops halfway, sees the flaw, and keeps coming back for 101 years until he learns that the self is not the body.

st.up.janaka_contest_yajnavalkya_cows.l: Ask your hard questions bravely, and give credit where it is due.
st.up.janaka_contest_yajnavalkya_cows.s: King Janaka offers a thousand cows to the wisest scholar. Yajnavalkya claims them and is challenged by one learned man after another. Gargi, the only woman, rises twice like a warrior with two arrows, then graciously tells the hall none of them can beat him. Yajnavalkya closes by asking what root a person grows from when cut down by death.
st.up.janaka_contest_yajnavalkya_cows.t: Gargi questions Yajnavalkya at Janaka's court

st.up.janaka_steps_down_from_throne.l: When every outer light fails, you still have your own.
st.up.janaka_steps_down_from_throne.s: Yajnavalkya asks the rich, learned King Janaka where he will go when he dies, and the king admits he does not know. Later Janaka asks what light a person lives by: sun, then moon, then fire, then voice, and when all are gone, the self is one's own light.
st.up.janaka_steps_down_from_throne.t: Janaka asks: what is our light?

st.up.maitreyi_what_would_i_do_with_weal.l: Wealth buys comfort; ask for what lasts.
st.up.maitreyi_what_would_i_do_with_weal.s: Before leaving home, Yajnavalkya offers to divide his property between his two wives. Maitreyi asks whether all the world's wealth would make her immortal, and when he says no, she asks for what he knows instead. He teaches her that we love husband, wife and children for the self shining in them.

st.up.maitreyi_you_have_confused_me.l: Wealth buys comfort; ask for what lasts.
st.up.maitreyi_you_have_confused_me.s: Before leaving home, Yajnavalkya offers to divide his property between his two wives. Maitreyi asks whether all the world's wealth would make her immortal, and when he says no, she asks for what he knows instead. He teaches her that we love husband, wife and children for the self shining in them.

st.up.man_from_gandhara.l: What is most real in you is unseen, everywhere, and the same in all.
st.up.man_from_gandhara.s: Uddalaka teaches his son through everyday experiments: a fast that dims the mind, a bird on a string, rivers merging in the sea, a banyan seed with nothing visible inside, salt dissolved in water, a blindfolded man finding his way home. Each lesson ends: 'That subtle essence is the self of all. You are that, Shvetaketu.'

st.up.nachiketa_questions_father.l: A child's honest question can show up an adult's empty gesture.
st.up.nachiketa_questions_father.s: A father makes a show of giving away all he owns, but the cows are old and dry. His young son Nachiketa keeps asking who he will be given to, until the father snaps, 'To Death!' The boy goes, and tells his father to keep his word.

st.up.nachiketa_refuses_bribes.l: Ask for peace with your family first, and don't trade the real question for comfort.
st.up.nachiketa_refuses_bribes.s: Death, away from home, keeps the boy waiting three days and offers three boons in apology. Nachiketa asks first that his father be calm and not angry with him, then for a sacred fire, then for the truth about death. Yama tempts him with sons, gold, long life and pleasures instead; the boy refuses them all.
st.up.nachiketa_refuses_bribes.t: The three boons and the refused fortune

st.up.nachiketa_three_nights_first_boon.l: Ask for peace with your family first, and don't trade the real question for comfort.
st.up.nachiketa_three_nights_first_boon.s: Death, away from home, keeps the boy waiting three days and offers three boons in apology. Nachiketa asks first that his father be calm and not angry with him, then for a sacred fire, then for the truth about death. Yama tempts him with sons, gold, long life and pleasures instead; the boy refuses them all.
st.up.nachiketa_three_nights_first_boon.t: The three boons and the refused fortune

st.up.narada_knows_everything_still_grie.l: Success and learning don't cure sadness; only the infinite does.
st.up.narada_knows_everything_still_grie.s: Narada, who has mastered every science of his day, comes to Sanatkumara and admits he is unhappy: he knows words, not himself. Sanatkumara leads him step by step from names up through action and joy to the infinite, teaching that happiness is found only in the vast, never in the small.

st.up.nidagha_after_the_pilgrimage.l: Naming how restless your mind is, is where peace begins.
st.up.nidagha_after_the_pilgrimage.s: Young Nidagha returns from pilgrimage disillusioned and pours out his heart to his teacher Ribhu: life is fleeting, the mind runs like a stray dog, craving gnaws every good quality, and mastering the mind is harder than drinking the ocean.

st.up.prashna_wait_a_year.l: Readiness matters, and a good teacher only claims what he knows.
st.up.prashna_wait_a_year.s: Six earnest seekers come to the sage Pippalada with questions. Instead of answering, he asks them to live with him for a year in discipline and faith, and only promises to answer what he actually knows.

st.up.satyakama_four_hundred_cows.l: Honesty about who you are is the best credential you can bring.
st.up.satyakama_four_hundred_cows.s: A boy who wants to study asks his mother about his father's lineage. She tells him frankly she does not know, and he repeats this word for word to the teacher. The teacher accepts him for his honesty, sends him off with 400 weak cows, and the boy returns years later with a thousand, having learned from nature along the way, yet still asks his teacher to teach him.

st.up.senses_quarrel.l: The quiet one everyone relies on often matters most.
st.up.senses_quarrel.s: Speech, sight, hearing and mind each claim to be the most important. Their father says the greatest is the one whose absence hurts the body most. Each leaves for a year and the body manages; when breath starts to leave, all the others are torn loose and beg it to stay.
st.up.senses_quarrel.t: The senses argue over who is greatest

st.up.shaunaka_householder_asks.l: Skills and degrees are real knowledge, but not the deepest kind.
st.up.shaunaka_householder_asks.s: A wealthy householder asks a sage what single thing, once known, explains everything. Angiras says all our sciences and rituals are the lower knowledge; the higher is knowing the imperishable. He warns against people wise in their own eyes and sends the seeker to a real teacher.
st.up.shaunaka_householder_asks.t: Shaunaka's question: two kinds of knowledge

st.up.shuka_at_janakas_gate.l: Steadiness is proved when neither neglect nor luxury moves you.
st.up.shuka_at_janakas_gate.s: Young Shuka, already wise, is sent by his father Vyasa to King Janaka. Janaka ignores him at the gate for seven days, then lets him wait in the courtyard seven more, then surrounds him with luxury for seven days. Shuka stays exactly the same throughout, and Janaka bows to him.

st.up.shvetaketu_comes_home_proud.l: Learning without humility misses the main thing.
st.up.shvetaketu_comes_home_proud.s: After twelve years of study, Shvetaketu returns home at twenty-four full of himself. His father gently asks whether he learned the one thing that makes everything else understood, and the son admits his teachers never taught it.

st.up.shvetaketu_fifteen_day_fast.l: What is most real in you is unseen, everywhere, and the same in all.
st.up.shvetaketu_fifteen_day_fast.s: Uddalaka teaches his son through everyday experiments: a fast that dims the mind, a bird on a string, rivers merging in the sea, a banyan seed with nothing visible inside, salt dissolved in water, a blindfolded man finding his way home. Each lesson ends: 'That subtle essence is the self of all. You are that, Shvetaketu.'

st.up.shvetaketu_jaivali_five_questions.l: A good parent admits what they don't know and goes on learning.
st.up.shvetaketu_jaivali_five_questions.s: Shvetaketu boasts that his father has taught him everything, then cannot answer a single one of a king's five questions. He runs home and blames his father, who honestly admits he does not know either, and goes to the king himself, refusing wealth and asking only to learn.
st.up.shvetaketu_jaivali_five_questions.t: Shvetaketu humbled at the king's court

st.up.shvetashvatara_who_governs_us.l: Refuge in God comes at the end of honest questioning, not instead of it.
st.up.shvetashvatara_who_governs_us.s: Seekers ask what causes the world and governs their joys and sorrows. Through meditation they come to see one Lord, Rudra-Shiva, hidden in every heart; the Upanishad moves from inquiry to recognition to a prayer of refuge (6.18) and ends on grace and love of God (6.21, 6.23).
st.up.shvetashvatara_who_governs_us.t: Shvetashvatara: from 'what governs our lives?' to refuge

st.up.sukesha_refuses_to_bluff.l: Saying 'I don't know' keeps you honest and keeps you learning.
st.up.sukesha_refuses_to_bluff.s: A prince once asked Sukesha a hard question. Rather than bluff, Sukesha said 'I do not know,' because whoever lies withers to the root. The prince drove off in silence, and Sukesha carried the question to his teacher.

st.up.tat_tvam_asi_seed_and_salt.l: What is most real in you is unseen, everywhere, and the same in all.
st.up.tat_tvam_asi_seed_and_salt.s: Uddalaka teaches his son through everyday experiments: a fast that dims the mind, a bird on a string, rivers merging in the sea, a banyan seed with nothing visible inside, salt dissolved in water, a blindfolded man finding his way home. Each lesson ends: 'That subtle essence is the self of all. You are that, Shvetaketu.'

st.up.two_birds.l: There is a calm witness in you that the anxious part can turn to.
st.up.two_birds.s: Two birds sit on one tree: one eats the fruit and grieves, the other simply watches. When the anxious bird sees the calm one beside it, its sorrow falls away. The section goes on to praise truth, effort and freedom from craving.

up_adhyatma.22.m: As moss pushed aside does not stay away even a moment, so illusion covers again even a wise person who turns away.
roles: Shows practice has to be kept up.
up_adhyatma.22.sa: यथापकृष्टं शैवालं क्षणमात्रं न तिष्ठति । आवृणोति तथा माया प्राज्ञं वापि पराङ्मुखम् ॥

up_adhyatma.54.m: Whether honoured by the good or harassed by the wicked, one who stays the same is called free while living.
roles: Shows the same inner state under honour and under harassment.
up_adhyatma.54.sa: साधुभिः पूज्यमानेऽस्मिन्पीड्यमानेऽपि दुर्जनैः । समभावो भवेद्यस्य स जीवन्मुक्त इष्यते ॥

up_adhyatma.60.m: Action that began before knowledge dawned is not destroyed by knowledge without yielding its fruit, like an arrow released at its target. An arrow loosed at what looked like a tiger does not stop when you see it is a cow; it flies on and strikes the target with force.
roles: Shows one bearing what was set going earlier.
up_adhyatma.60.sa: ज्ञानोदयात्पुरारब्धं कर्म ज्ञानान्न नश्यति । अदत्त्वा स्वफलं लक्ष्यमुद्दिश्योत्सृष्टबाणवत् ॥ व्याघ्रबुद्ध्या विनिर्मुक्तो बाणः पश्चात्तु गोमतौ । न तिष्ठति भिनत्त्येव लक्ष्यं वेगेन निर्भरम् ॥

up_aitareya.33.m: When he cares for the child from birth onward, he is caring for himself, for the continuation of these worlds; that is how they continue. That is his second birth.
roles: The child is not other than oneself.
up_aitareya.33.sa: स यत्कुमारं जन्मनोऽग्रेऽधिभावयत्यात्मानमेव तद्भावयत्येषं लोकानां सन्तत्या । एवं सन्तता हीमे लोकास्तदस्य द्वितीयं जन्म ॥

up_aitareya.34.m: This self of his, the child, is put in his place to carry on good works. Then his other self, the parent, having done what was to be done and grown old, departs; departing from here, he is born again. That is his third birth.
roles: Shows the child stands in the parent's place for what is good.
up_aitareya.34.sa: सोऽस्यायमात्मा पुण्येभ्यः कर्मभ्यः प्रतिधीयते । अथास्यायामितर आत्मा कृतकृत्यो वयोगतः प्रैति । स इतः प्रयन्नेव पुनर्जायते तदस्य तृतीयं जन्म ॥

up_brihadaranyak.188.m: Maitreyi said: 'Sir, if this whole earth full of wealth were mine, would I become immortal by it?' 'No,' said Yajnavalkya. 'Your life would be like the life of the well-off. There is no hope of immortality through wealth.'
roles: Separates what wealth can do from what it cannot.
up_brihadaranyak.188.sa: सा होवाच मैत्रेयी यन्नु म इयं भगोः सर्वा पृथिवी वित्तेन पूर्णा स्यात् कथं तेनामृता स्यामिति । नेति होवाच याज्ञवल्क्यो यथैवोपकरणवतां जीवितं तथैव ते जीवितꣳ स्यादमृतत्वस्य तु नाऽऽशाऽस्ति वित्तेनेति ॥

scene.s: Before leaving home, Yajnavalkya offers to divide his property between his two wives. Maitreyi asks whether all the world's wealth would make her immortal, and when he says no, she asks for what he knows instead. He teaches her that we love husband, wife and children for the self shining in them.

up_brihadaranyak.189.m: Maitreyi said: 'What should I do with that which will not make me immortal? Tell me, sir, what you know.'
roles: Models asking of any gain will this give me what I actually want.
up_brihadaranyak.189.sa: सा होवाच मैत्रेयी येनाहं नामृता स्यां किमहं तेन कुर्याम् । यदेव भगवान्वेद तदेव मे ब्रूहीति ॥

scene.s: Before leaving home, Yajnavalkya offers to divide his property between his two wives. Maitreyi asks whether all the world's wealth would make her immortal, and when he says no, she asks for what he knows instead. He teaches her that we love husband, wife and children for the self shining in them.

up_brihadaranyak.191.m: He said: 'It is not for the love of the husband that a husband is dear, but for the love of the self that a husband is dear. It is not for the love of the wife that a wife is dear, but for the love of the self. It is not for the love of the sons that sons are dear, but for the love of the self that sons are dear.'
roles: Shows the self as what is dearest and must be known.
up_brihadaranyak.191.sa: स होवाच न वा अरे पत्युः कामाय पतिः प्रियो भवत्यात्मनस्तु कामाय पतिः प्रियो भवति । न वा अरे जायायै कामाय जाया प्रिया भवत्यात्मनस्तु कामाय जाया प्रिया भवति । न वा अरे पुत्राणां कामाय पुत्राः प्रिया भवन्त्यात्मनस्तु कामाय पुत्राः प्रिया भवन्ति ।

scene.s: Before leaving home, Yajnavalkya offers to divide his property between his two wives. Maitreyi asks whether all the world's wealth would make her immortal, and when he says no, she asks for what he knows instead. He teaches her that we love husband, wife and children for the self shining in them.

up_brihadaranyak.283.m: The desire for sons is the desire for wealth, and the desire for wealth is the desire for worlds; both are just desires. So a wise man, having done with learning, should seek to live like a child. Having done with both childlike simplicity and learning, he becomes a sage; having done with both silence and its absence, he becomes a true knower.
roles: Shows the knower rising above all three.
up_brihadaranyak.283.sa: या ह्येव पुत्रैषणा सा वित्तैषणा या वित्तैषणा सा लोकैषणोभे ह्येते एषणे एव भवतस्तस्माद्ब्राह्मणः पाण्डित्यं निर्विद्य बाल्येन तिष्ठासेत् । बाल्यं च पाण्डित्यं च निर्विद्याथ मुनिरमौनं च मौनं च निर्विद्याथ ब्राह्मणः ।

scene.s: King Janaka offers a thousand cows to the wisest scholar. Yajnavalkya claims them and is challenged by one learned man after another. Gargi, the only woman, rises twice like a warrior with two arrows, then graciously tells the hall none of them can beat him. Yajnavalkya closes by asking what root a person grows from when cut down by death.
scene.t: Gargi questions Yajnavalkya at Janaka's court

up_brihadaranyak.323.m: She said: 'Yajnavalkya, as a warrior from Kashi or Videha strings his unstrung bow and rises with two piercing arrows in hand, so I rise before you with two questions. Answer them for me.' 'Ask, Gargi.'
roles: She speaks as an equal to the champion of the debate.
up_brihadaranyak.323.sa: सा होवाचाहं वै त्वा याज्ञवल्क्य यथा काश्यो वा वैदेहो वोग्रपुत्र उज्ज्यं धनुरधिज्यं कृत्वा द्वौ बाणवन्तौ सपत्नातिव्याधिनौ हस्ते कृत्वोपोत्तिष्ठेदेवमेवाहं त्वा द्वाभ्यां प्रश्नाभ्यामुपोदस्थाम् । तौ मे ब्रूहीति । पृच्छ गार्गीति ॥

scene.s: King Janaka offers a thousand cows to the wisest scholar. Yajnavalkya claims them and is challenged by one learned man after another. Gargi, the only woman, rises twice like a warrior with two arrows, then graciously tells the hall none of them can beat him. Yajnavalkya closes by asking what root a person grows from when cut down by death.
scene.t: Gargi questions Yajnavalkya at Janaka's court

up_brihadaranyak.332.m: Gargi, whoever in this world performs rituals, makes offerings and practises austerity for many thousands of years without knowing this imperishable, all that work of his comes to an end. Whoever leaves this world without knowing this imperishable is pitiable. Whoever leaves this world knowing it is a true knower.
roles: Makes knowing the imperishable the one thing not to miss.
up_brihadaranyak.332.sa: यो वा एतदक्षरं गार्ग्यविदित्वाऽस्मिꣳल्लोके जुहोति यजते तपस्तप्यते बहूनि वर्षसहस्राण्यन्तवदेवास्य तद्भवति लोको भवति यो वा एतदक्षरं गार्ग्यविदित्वाऽस्माल्लोकात्प्रैति स कृपणोऽथ य एतदक्षरं गार्गि विदित्वाऽस्माल्लोकात्प्रैति स ब्राह्मणः ॥

Gargi, the only woman, rises twice like a warrior with two arrows, then graciously tells the hall none of them can beat him. Yajnavalkya closes by asking what root a person grows from when cut down by death.
scene.t: Gargi questions Yajnavalkya at Janaka's court

up_brihadaranyak.334.m: She said: 'Venerable brahmins, count it a great thing if you get away from him with a bow. None of you will ever defeat him in talk about Brahman.' Then Gargi Vachaknavi fell silent.
roles: Shows honesty about who is better as strength.
up_brihadaranyak.334.sa: सा होवाच ब्राह्मणा भगवन्तस्तदेव बहु मन्येध्वं यदस्मान्नमस्कारेण मुच्येध्वं न वै जातु युष्माकमिमं कश्चिद्ब्रह्मोद्यं जेतेति ततो ह वाचक्नव्युपरराम ॥

scene.s: King Janaka offers a thousand cows to the wisest scholar. Yajnavalkya claims them and is challenged by one learned man after another. Gargi, the only woman, rises twice like a warrior with two arrows, then graciously tells the hall none of them can beat him. Yajnavalkya closes by asking what root a person grows from when cut down by death.
scene.t: Gargi questions Yajnavalkya at Janaka's court

up_brihadaranyak.387.m: If a tree is cut down, it grows again from its root, newer still. When a mortal is cut down by death, from what root does he grow again?
roles: Shows the question about death asked without an answer attached.
up_brihadaranyak.387.sa: यद्वृक्षो वृक्णो रोहति मूलान्नवतरः पुनः मर्त्यः स्विन्मृत्युना वृक्णः कस्मान्मूलात्प्ररोहति ॥

scene.s: King Janaka offers a thousand cows to the wisest scholar. Yajnavalkya claims them and is challenged by one learned man after another. Gargi, the only woman, rises twice like a warrior with two arrows, then graciously tells the hall none of them can beat him. Yajnavalkya closes by asking what root a person grows from when cut down by death.
scene.t: Gargi questions Yajnavalkya at Janaka's court

up_brihadaranyak.418.m: He said: 'Your Majesty, as a man setting out on a long journey would take a chariot or a ship, so you have equipped yourself with these teachings. You are honoured and wealthy, you have studied the Vedas and heard the Upanishads. When you leave this world, where will you go?' 'I do not know, sir, where I shall go.' 'Then I will tell you where you will go.' 'Tell me, sir.'
roles: Shows a king who has everything admitting plainly I do not know.
up_brihadaranyak.418.sa: स होवाच यथा वै सम्राण् महान्तमध्वानमेष्यन्रथं वा नावं वा समाददीतैवमेवैताभिरुपनिषद्भिः समाहितात्माऽस्यसि एवं वृन्दारक आढ्यः सन्नधीतवेद उक्तोपनिषत्क इतो विमुच्यमानः क्व गमिष्यसीति । नाहं तद् भगवन् वेद यत्र गमिष्यामीत्यथ वै तेऽहं तद्वक्ष्यामि यत्र गमिष्यसीति । ब्रवीतु भगवानिति ॥

scene.s: Yajnavalkya asks the rich, learned King Janaka where he will go when he dies, and the king admits he does not know. Later Janaka asks what light a person lives by: sun, then moon, then fire, then voice, and when all are gone, the self is one's own light.
scene.t: Janaka asks: what is our light?

up_brihadaranyak.429.m: 'When the sun has set, Yajnavalkya, and the moon has set, and the fire has gone out, what light does a person have?' 'Speech is then his light; for when one cannot even see one's own hand, where a voice is heard, there one goes.' 'And when speech too is silent?' 'Then the self is his light. By the light of the self he sits, goes about, works and returns.'
roles: Points to the awareness that remains when sun, moon, fire and speech are all gone.
up_brihadaranyak.429.sa: अस्तमित आदित्ये याज्ञवल्क्य चन्द्रमस्यस्तमिते शान्तेऽग्नौ किञ्ज्योतिरेवायं पुरुष इति । वागेवास्य ज्योतिर्भवतीति वाचैवायं ज्योतिषास्ते पल्ययते कर्म कुरुते विपल्येतीति । तस्माद्वै सम्राड् अपि यत्र स्वः पाणिर्न विनिर्ज्ञायतेऽथ यत्र वागुच्चरत्युपैव तत्रन्येतीत्येवमेवैतद् याज्ञवल्क्य ॥ अस्तमित आदित्ये याज्ञवल्क्य चन्द्रमस्यस्तमिते शान्तेऽग्नौ शान्तायां वाचि किञ्ज्योतिरेवायं पुरुष इत्यात्मैवास्य ज्योतिर्भवत्यात्मनैवायं ज्योतिषाऽऽस्ते पल्ययते कर्म कुरुते विपल्येतीति ॥

up_brihadaranyak.473.m: As a caterpillar, reaching the end of a blade of grass, takes hold of another and draws itself over to it, so this self, having left this body behind and let go of ignorance, takes hold of another support and draws itself over.
roles: Shows the self passing over and the body left behind.

up_brihadaranyak.474.m: As a goldsmith takes a piece of gold and fashions another form, newer and more beautiful, so this self, leaving this body behind and letting go of ignorance, makes for itself another form, newer and more beautiful.
roles: Names the self as gold and the body as its shape.
up_brihadaranyak.474.sa: तद्यथा पेशस्कारी पेशसो मात्रामपादायान्यन्नवतरं कल्याणतरꣳ रूपं तनुत एवमेवायमात्मेदꣳ शरीरं निहत्याविद्यां गमयित्वाऽन्यन्नवतरं कल्याणतरꣳ रूपं कुरुते पित्र्यं वा गान्धर्वं वा दैवं वा प्राजापत्यं वा ब्राह्मं वाऽन्येषां वा भूतानाम् ॥

up_brihadaranyak.477.m: And so they say: a person is made of desire. As his desire is, so is his will; as his will is, so is his deed; and whatever deed he does, that he becomes.
roles: Shows choosing what to want is where change starts.
up_brihadaranyak.477.sa: अथो खल्वाहुः काममय एवायं पुरुष इति स यथाकामो भवति तत्क्रतुर्भवति यत्क्रतुर्भवति तत्कर्म कुरुते यत्कर्म कुरुते तदभिसम्पद्यते ॥

up_brihadaranyak.486.m: If a person knew the self as 'I am this', then wanting what, and for whose sake, would he fret after the body?
roles: Names the self as I am this.
up_brihadaranyak.486.sa: आत्मानं चेद्विजानीयादयमस्मीति पूरुषः किमिच्छन्कस्य कामाय शरीरमनुसञ्ज्वरेत् ॥

up_brihadaranyak.488.m: While we are still here, we may know it. If we do not, great is the loss. Those who know it become immortal; the rest go only to sorrow.
roles: Makes knowing oneself the thing not to postpone.
up_brihadaranyak.488.sa: इहैव सन्तोऽथ विद्मस्तद्वयं न चेदवेदिर्महती विनष्टिः । ये तद्विदुरमृतास्ते भवन्त्यथेतरे दुःखमेवापियन्ति ॥

up_brihadaranyak.495.m: Knowing that one alone, let the wise seeker cultivate understanding. Let him not brood over many words, for that only wearies the voice.
roles: Names fewer words and one object of attention.
up_brihadaranyak.495.sa: तमेव धीरो विज्ञाय प्रज्ञां कुर्वीत ब्राह्मणः । नानुध्यायाद्बहूञ्छब्दान् वाचो विग्लापनꣳ हि तदिति ॥

up_brihadaranyak.501.m: This is said in a verse: This eternal greatness of the knower neither grows by deeds nor shrinks. Let one know its nature; knowing it, one is not stained by wrong action. So one who knows this, calm, self-controlled, withdrawn, patient and collected, sees the self in himself and sees everything as the self.
roles: Shows seeing the self in oneself and everything as the self.
up_brihadaranyak.501.sa: तदेतदृचाभ्युक्तम् । एष नित्यो महिमा ब्राह्मणस्य न वर्धते कर्मणा नो कनीयान् । तस्यैव स्यात् पदवित्तं विदित्वा न लिप्यते कर्मणा पापकेनेति । तस्मादेवंविच्छान्तो दान्त उपरतस्तितिक्षुः समाहितो भूत्वाऽऽत्मन्येवाऽऽत्मानं पश्यति सर्वमात्मानं पश्यति

up_brihadaranyak.533.m: That is whole; this is whole. From the whole, the whole arises. Taking the whole from the whole, the whole remains. Om. Brahman is space, the ancient space, the airy space, said the son of Kauravyayani. This is the Veda the brahmins know; by it one knows what is to be known.
roles: This, the self here, is as whole as that.
up_brihadaranyak.533.sa: ॐ पूर्णमदः पूर्णमिदं पूर्णात्पूर्णमुदच्यते । पूर्णस्य पूर्णमादाय पूर्णमेवावशिष्यते । ॐ३ खं ब्रह्म खं पुराणं वायुरं खमिति ह स्माऽऽह कौरव्यायणीपुत्रो । वेदोऽयम्ं ब्राह्मणा विदुर्वेदैनेन यद्वेदितव्यम् ॥

up_brihadaranyak.534.m: The gods, humans and demons, the three children of Prajapati, lived with their father as students. The gods asked for teaching; he said the syllable 'Da' and asked if they understood. 'Be self-controlled (damyata),' they said. 'Yes.' The humans asked; 'Da.' 'Give (datta),' they said. 'Yes.' The demons asked; 'Da.' 'Be compassionate (dayadhvam),' they said. 'Yes.' The divine voice of thunder repeats it: Da Da Da: be self-controlled, give, be compassionate. One should learn these three: self-control, giving, compassion.
up_brihadaranyak.534.sa: त्रयाः प्राजापत्याः प्रजापतौ पितरि ब्रह्मचर्यमूषुर्देवा मनुष्या असुरा उषित्वा ब्रह्मचर्यं देवा ऊचुर्ब्रवीतु नो भवानिति । तेभ्यो हैतदक्षरमुवाच द इति व्यज्ञासिष्टा३ इति । व्यज्ञासिष्मेति होचुर्दाम्यतेति न आत्थेत्योमिति होवाच व्यज्ञासिष्टेति ॥ अथ हैनं मनुष्या ऊचुर्ब्रवीतु नो भवानिति । तेभ्यो हैतदेवाक्षरमुवाच द इति व्यज्ञासिष्टा३ इति । व्यज्ञासिष्मेति होचुर्दत्तेति न आत्थेत्योमिति होवाच व्यज्ञासिष्टेति ॥ अथ हैनमसुरा ऊचुर्ब्रवीतु नो भवानिति । तेभ्यो हैतदेवाक्षरमुवाच द इति व्यज्ञासिष्टा३ इति । व्यज्ञासिष्मेति होचुर्दयध्वमिति न आत्थेत्योमिति होवाच व्यज्ञासिष्टेति । तदेतदेवैषा दैवी वागनुवदति स्तनयित्नुर्द द द इति दाम्यत दत्त दयध्वमिति । तदेतत्त्रयꣳ शिक्षेद् दमं दानं दयामिति ॥

up_brihadaranyak.56.m: Now the chanting of the purifying verses. When the priest begins the hymn, one should recite: From the unreal lead me to the real. From darkness lead me to light. From death lead me to immortality.
roles: Shows the prayer not claiming to find the way alone.
up_brihadaranyak.56.sa: अथातः पवमानानामेवाभ्यारोहः । स वै खलु प्रस्तोता साम प्रस्तौति । स यत्र प्रस्तुयात् तदेतानि जपेदसतो मा सद् गमय तमसो मा ज्योतिर्गमय मृत्योर्माऽमृतं गमयेति ।

up_brihadaranyak.62.m: He was afraid; that is why one who is alone is afraid. Then he thought: 'Since there is nothing but me, what am I afraid of?' At that his fear left him. What was there to fear? Fear arises only from a second.
roles: Shows fearlessness is reached by looking, not by bravery.
up_brihadaranyak.62.sa: सोऽबिभेत् तस्मादेकाकी बिभेति । स हायमीक्षां चक्रे यन्मदन्यन्नास्ति कस्मान्नु बिभेमीति । तत एवास्य भयं वीयाय । कस्माद्ध्यभेष्यत् द्वितीयाद्वै भयं भवति ॥

up_brihadaranyak.86.m: Still he did not flourish. So he created a higher form, dharma. Dharma is the power over power; nothing is higher than dharma. Through dharma even a weak man can stand up to a strong one, as with the help of a king. That dharma is truth. So people say of one who speaks truth, 'He speaks dharma,' and of one who speaks dharma, 'He speaks truth.' Both are the same.
roles: Shows standing on what is true and right, as one would stand behind a king.
up_brihadaranyak.86.sa: स नैव व्यभवत् तच्छ्रेयो रूपमत्यसृजत धर्मम् । तदेतत्क्षत्रस्य क्षत्रं यद्धर्मस्तस्माद्धर्मात् परं नास्त्यथो अबलीयान् बलीयाꣳसमाशꣳसते धर्मेण यथा राज्ञैवम् । यो वै स धर्मः सत्यं वै तत् तस्मात्सत्यं वदन्तमाहुर्धर्मं वदतीति धर्मं वा वदन्तꣳ सत्यं वदतीत्येतद्ध्येवैतदुभयं भवति ॥

up_brihadaranyak.92.m: By housing people and giving them food, he becomes a world for people. By finding grass and water for animals, he becomes a world for animals. When beasts, birds and even ants live off his house, he becomes a world for them.
roles: Shows care reaching down to birds and ants.
up_brihadaranyak.92.sa: यन्मनुष्यान्वासयते यदेभ्योऽशनं ददाति तेन मनुष्याणामथ यत्पशुभ्यस्तृणोदकं विन्दति तेन पशूनां यदस्य गृहेषु श्वापदा वयाꣳस्या पिपीलिकाभ्य उपजीवन्ति तेन तेषां लोको

up_chhandogya.10.m: Both the one who knows and the one who does not know perform the act. But knowledge and ignorance are different. Whatever is done with knowledge, with faith and with inner understanding becomes more powerful.
roles: Shows faith named as part of what gives an act its strength.
up_chhandogya.10.sa: तेनोभौ कुरुतो यश्चैतदेवं वेद यश्च न वेद । नाना तु विद्या चाविद्या च यदेव विद्यया करोति श्रद्धयोपनिषदा तदेव वीर्यवत्तरं भवतीति खल्वेतस्यैवाक्षरस्योपव्याख्यानं भवति ॥

up_chhandogya.247.m: All this is Brahman; from it all arises, into it all dissolves, in it all breathes; so one should meditate on it calmly. A person is made of resolve. As one's resolve is in this world, so one becomes on departing. So let one form a resolve.
roles: Cultivates what you settle your conviction on as what you become.
up_chhandogya.247.sa: सर्वं खल्विदं ब्रह्म तज्जलानिति शान्त उपासीत । अथ खलु क्रतुमयः पुरुषो यथाक्रतुरस्मिꣳल्लोके पुरुषो भवति तथेतः प्रेत्य भवति स क्रतुं कुर्वीत ॥

up_chhandogya.268.m: And discipline, generosity, straightforwardness, non-harming and truthful speech: these are its gifts to the priests.
roles: Discipline is shown as the first of them.
up_chhandogya.268.sa: अथ यत्तपो दानमार्जवमहिꣳसा सत्यवचनमिति ता अस्य दक्षिणाः ॥

up_chhandogya.308.m: He said to him: 'No one but a true brahmin could speak so plainly. Bring fuel, dear one; I will take you as a student, for you have not swerved from the truth.' Having initiated him, he picked out four hundred thin, weak cows and said, 'Follow these, dear one.'
roles: Honesty about oneself is honoured as nobility.
up_chhandogya.308.sa: तꣳ होवाच नैतदब्राह्मणो विवक्तुमर्हति समिधꣳ सोम्याहरोप त्वा नेष्ये न सत्यादगा इति तमुपनीय कृशानामबलानां चतुःशता गा निराकृत्योवाचेमाः सोम्यानुसंव्रजेति

scene.s: A boy who wants to study asks his mother about his father's lineage. She tells him frankly she does not know, and he repeats this word for word to the teacher. The teacher accepts him for his honesty, sends him off with 400 weak cows, and the boy returns years later with a thousand, having learned from nature along the way, yet still asks his teacher to teach him.

up_chhandogya.309.m: As he drove them off he said, 'I will not return until they are a thousand.' He lived away for years, until they had become a thousand.
roles: Shows years of quiet work on an unpromising start.
up_chhandogya.309.sa: ता अभिप्रस्थापयन्नुवाच नासहस्रेणावर्तेयेति स ह वर्षगणं प्रोवास ता यदा सहस्रꣳ सम्पेदुः ॥

scene.s: A boy who wants to study asks his mother about his father's lineage. She tells him frankly she does not know, and he repeats this word for word to the teacher. The teacher accepts him for his honesty, sends him off with 400 weak cows, and the boy returns years later with a thousand, having learned from nature along the way, yet still asks his teacher to teach him.

up_chhandogya.326.m: 'You shine like one who knows Brahman, dear one. Who has taught you?' 'Others than men,' he admitted. 'But I wish that you, sir, would teach me, for I have heard from people like you that knowledge learned from a teacher best reaches its goal.' So the teacher taught him that very knowledge, and nothing was left out.
roles: Shows knowing a great deal does not end the asking.
up_chhandogya.326.sa: ब्रह्मविदिव वै सोम्य भासि को नु त्वानुशशासेत्यन्ये मनुष्येभ्य इति ह प्रतिजज्ञे भगवाꣳस्त्वेव मे कामे ब्रूयात् ॥ श्रुतꣳह्येव मे भगवद्दृशेभ्य आचार्याद्धैव विद्या विदिता साधिष्ठं प्रापतीति तस्मै हैतदेवोवाचात्र ह न किंचन वीयायेति वीयायेति ॥

scene.s: A boy who wants to study asks his mother about his father's lineage. She tells him frankly she does not know, and he repeats this word for word to the teacher. The teacher accepts him for his honesty, sends him off with 400 weak cows, and the boy returns years later with a thousand, having learned from nature along the way, yet still asks his teacher to teach him.

up_chhandogya.368.m: The senses quarrelled about who was best, each saying, 'I am best, I am best.' They went to their father Prajapati and asked, 'Sir, who is the best of us?' He said, 'The one whose departure leaves the body looking worst off is the best among you.'
roles: Shows worth measured by what depends on you.
up_chhandogya.368.sa: अथ ह प्राणा अहꣳश्रेयसि व्यूदिरेऽहꣳश्रेयानस्म्यहꣳ श्रेयानस्मीति ॥ ते ह प्राणाः प्रजापतिं पितरमेत्योचुर्भगवन्को नः श्रेष्ठ इति तान्होवाच यस्मिन्व उत्क्रान्ते शरीरं पापिष्ठतरमिव दृश्येत स वः श्रेष्ठ इति ॥

scene.s: Speech, sight, hearing and mind each claim to be the most important. Their father says the greatest is the one whose absence hurts the body most. Each leaves for a year and the body manages; when breath starts to leave, all the others are torn loose and beg it to stay.
scene.t: The senses argue over who is greatest

up_chhandogya.391.m: 'That fellow of the warrior class asked me five questions, and I could not answer even one.' The father said, 'As you have put them to me, I do not know a single one of them. If I had known them, how could I not have told you?'
roles: The father goes to learn it himself.
up_chhandogya.391.sa: पञ्च मा राजन्यबन्धुः प्रश्नानप्राक्षीत्तेषां नैकंचनाशकं विवक्तुमिति स होवाच यथा मा त्वं तदैतानवदो यथाहमेषां नैकंचन वेद यद्यहमिमानवेदिष्यं कथं ते नावक्ष्यमिति ॥

scene.s: Shvetaketu boasts that his father has taught him everything, then cannot answer a single one of a king's five questions. He runs home and blames his father, who honestly admits he does not know either, and goes to the king himself, refusing wealth and asking only to learn.
scene.t: Shvetaketu humbled at the king's court

up_chhandogya.393.m: He said, 'Let human wealth remain with you, O king. Tell me the very words you spoke to my son.' The king was troubled.
roles: Shows asking for the very words spoken to his son.
up_chhandogya.393.sa: स होवाच तवैव राजन्मानुषं वित्तं यामेव कुमारस्यान्ते वाचमभाषथास्तामेव मे ब्रूहीति स ह कृच्छ्री बभूव ॥

scene.s: Shvetaketu boasts that his father has taught him everything, then cannot answer a single one of a king's five questions. He runs home and blames his father, who honestly admits he does not know either, and goes to the king himself, refusing wealth and asking only to learn.
scene.t: Shvetaketu humbled at the king's court

up_chhandogya.419.m: He thought: 'These great householders, great scholars, will question me, and I will not be able to answer everything. Let me direct them to another teacher.'
roles: Shows knowing the edge of one's knowledge and acting on it.
up_chhandogya.419.sa: स ह सम्पादयांचकार प्रक्ष्यन्ति मामिमे महाशाला महाश्रोत्रियास्तेभ्यो न सर्वमिव प्रतिपत्स्ये हन्ताहमन्यमभ्यनुशासानीति ॥

scene.s: Five great scholars come to Uddalaka to learn. Knowing he cannot answer everything, he takes them to King Ashvapati instead. The king proudly says his kingdom has no thieves or drunkards and offers gifts, but the scholars politely insist on the purpose they came for.
scene.t: Five scholars go to King Ashvapati

up_chhandogya.423.m: They said: 'A person should state the very purpose for which he has come. You know the universal self; teach that to us.'
roles: Keeps to the reason one came.
up_chhandogya.423.sa: ते होचुर्येन हैवार्थेन पुरुषश्चरेत्तꣳहैव वदेदात्मानमेवेमं वैश्वानरꣳ सम्प्रत्यध्येषि तमेव नौ ब्रूहीति ॥

up_chhandogya.455.m: He went at twelve and returned at twenty-four, having studied all the Vedas, conceited, proud of his learning, stiff. His father said: 'Shvetaketu, since you are so conceited, so proud of your learning, so stiff, did you ask for that teaching by which the unheard becomes heard, the unthought becomes thought, the unknown becomes known?' 'How could there be such a teaching, sir?'
up_chhandogya.455.sa: स ह द्वादशवर्ष उपेत्य चतुर्विꣳशतिवर्षः सर्वान्वेदानधीत्य महामना अनूचानमानी स्तब्ध एयाय तꣳह पितोवाच ॥ श्वेतकेतो यन्नु सोम्येदं महामना अनूचानमानी स्तब्धोऽस्युत तमादेशमप्राक्ष्यः येनाश्रुतꣳ श्रुतं भवत्यमतं मतमविज्ञातं विज्ञातमिति कथं नु भगवः स आदेशो भवतीति ॥

scene.s: After twelve years of study, Shvetaketu returns home at twenty-four full of himself. His father gently asks whether he learned the one thing that makes everything else understood, and the son admits his teachers never taught it.

up_chhandogya.489.m: 'As a single ember the size of a firefly, left from a great fire, can be fed with straw and made to blaze and burn far more, so, dear one, of your sixteen parts one was left. Fed with food, it blazed up, and with it you now recall the Vedas. For the mind is made of food, breath of water, speech of heat.' And he understood.
roles: Shows one small ember is enough to rebuild from.
up_chhandogya.489.sa: तꣳ होवाच यथा सोम्य महतोऽभ्याहितस्यैकमङ्गारं खद्योतमात्रं परिशिष्टं तं तृणैरुपसमाधाय प्राज्वलयेत्तेन ततोऽपि बहु दहेत् ॥ एवꣳ सोम्य ते षोडशानां कलानामेका कलातिशिष्टाभूत्सान्नेनोपसमाहिता प्राज्वाली तयैतर्हि वेदाननुभवस्यन्नमयꣳहि सोम्य मन आपोमयः प्राणस्तेजोमयी वागिति तद्धास्य विजज्ञाविति विजज्ञाविति ॥

up_chhandogya.492.m: As a bird tied by a string flies in every direction and, finding no resting place anywhere else, settles down at the very place it is tied, so, dear one, the mind flies in every direction and, finding no resting place anywhere else, settles down on the breath; for the mind is tied to the breath.
roles: Shows rest where the mind is already tied.
up_chhandogya.492.sa: स यथा शकुनिः सूत्रेण प्रबद्धो दिशं दिशं पतित्वान्यत्रायतनमलब्ध्वा बन्धनमेवोपश्रयत एवमेव खलु सोम्य तन्मनो दिशं दिशं पतित्वान्यत्रायतनमलब्ध्वा प्राणमेवोपश्रयते प्राणबन्धनꣳ हि सोम्य मन इति ॥

up_chhandogya.498.m: That which is the subtle essence: this whole world has it as its self. That is the truth. That is the self. That you are, Shvetaketu. 'Teach me more, sir.' 'So be it, dear one.'
roles: The plainest statement of identity in the Upanishads.
up_chhandogya.498.sa: स य एषोऽणिमैतदात्म्यमिदꣳ सर्वं तत्सत्यꣳ स आत्मा तत्त्वमसि श्वेतकेतो इति भूय एव मा भगवान्विज्ञापयत्विति तथा सोम्येति होवाच ॥

up_chhandogya.503.m: These rivers, dear one, flow, the eastern ones to the east and the western ones to the west. From the sea they come and into the sea they go, and become the sea itself. There they do not know, 'I am this river, I am that one.'
roles: Names all beings coming from one Being.
up_chhandogya.503.sa: इमाः सोम्य नद्यः पुरस्तात्प्राच्यः स्यन्दन्ते पश्चात्प्रतीच्यस्ताः समुद्रात्समुद्रमेवापियन्ति स समुद्र एव भवति ता यथा तत्र न विदुरियमहमस्मीयमहमस्मीति ॥

up_chhandogya.508.m: 'Know it to be just so, dear one,' he said. 'This body dies when life has left it; life itself does not die. That which is the subtle essence, this whole world has it as its self. That is the truth. That is the self. That you are, Shvetaketu.'
roles: Shows the tree lesson: life withdraws from a branch and the branch dries, but life is not what dried.
up_chhandogya.508.sa: एवमेव खलु सोम्य विद्धीति होवाच जीवापेतं वाव किलेदं म्रियते न जीवो म्रियते इति स य एषोऽणिमैतदात्म्यमिदꣳ सर्वं तत्सत्यꣳ स आत्मा तत्त्वमसि श्वेतकेतो इति भूय एव मा भगवान्विज्ञापयत्विति तथा सोम्येति होवाच ॥

up_chhandogya.509.m: 'Bring a fig from the banyan tree.' 'Here it is, sir.' 'Break it.' 'It is broken, sir.' 'What do you see?' 'These tiny seeds, sir.' 'Break one of them.' 'It is broken, sir.' 'What do you see?' 'Nothing at all, sir.' He said: 'That subtle essence you cannot see, dear one: from that very essence this great banyan stands. Have faith, dear one.'
roles: Names the father asking for trust exactly where the eye gives out.
up_chhandogya.509.sa: न्यग्रोधफलमत आहरेतीदं भगव इति भिन्द्धीति भिन्नं भगव इति किमत्र पश्यसीत्यण्व्य इवेमा धाना भगव इत्यासामङ्गैकां भिन्द्धीति भिन्ना भगव इति किमत्र पश्यसीति न किंचन भगव इति ॥ तꣳ होवाच यं वै सोम्यैतमणिमानं न निभालयस एतस्य वै सोम्यैषोऽणिम्न एवं महान्यग्रोधस्तिष्ठति श्रद्धत्स्व सोम्येति ॥

up_chhandogya.512.m: 'Put this salt in water and come to me in the morning.' He did so. The father said, 'Bring me the salt you put in the water last night.' He felt for it and could not find it, for it had dissolved. 'Sip from the top. How is it?' 'Salty.' 'From the middle?' 'Salty.' 'From the bottom?' 'Salty.' 'Throw it away and come to me.' He did, and said, 'It is always there.' The father said, 'You do not see it here, dear one, yet it is right here.'
roles: Shows being pervading this very body as salt pervades the water.
up_chhandogya.512.sa: लवणमेतदुदकेऽवधायाथ मा प्रातरुपसीदथा इति स ह तथा चकार तꣳ होवाच यद्दोषा लवणमुदकेऽवाधा अङ्ग तदाहरेति तद्धावमृश्य न विवेद ॥ यथा विलीनमेवाङ्गास्यान्तादाचामेति कथमिति लवणमिति मध्यादाचामेति कथमिति लवणमित्यन्तादाचामेति कथमिति लवणमित्यभिप्रास्यैतदथ मोपसीदथा इति तद्ध तथा चकार तच्छश्वत्संवर्तते तꣳ होवाचात्र वाव किल तत्सोम्य न निभालयसेऽत्रैव किलेति ॥

up_chhandogya.515.m: As a man brought blindfolded from Gandhara and left in a deserted place might wander east or north or south, crying, 'I was brought here blindfolded and left blindfolded,' and someone removes his blindfold and says, 'Gandhara is that way, go that way,' and asking from village to village, informed and sensible, he reaches Gandhara; so a person who has a teacher comes to know.
roles: Shows accepting direction from one who knows the way.
up_chhandogya.515.sa: यथा सोम्य पुरुषं गन्धारेभ्योऽभिनद्धाक्षमानीय तं ततोऽतिजने विसृजेत्स यथा तत्र प्राङ्वोदङ्वाधराङ्वा प्रत्यङ्वा प्रध्मायीताभिनद्धाक्ष आनीतोऽभिनद्धाक्षो विसृष्टः ॥ तस्य यथाभिनहनं प्रमुच्य प्रब्रूयादेतां दिशं गन्धारा एतां दिशं व्रजेति स ग्रामाद्ग्रामं पृच्छन्पण्डितो मेधावी गन्धारानेवोपसम्पद्येतैवमेवेहाचार्यवान्पुरुषो वेद तस्य तावदेव चिरं यावन्न विमोक्ष्येऽथ सम्पत्स्य इति ॥

up_chhandogya.518.m: Relatives gather around a man who is gravely ill and ask, 'Do you know me? Do you know me?' As long as his speech has not merged into mind, mind into breath, breath into heat and heat into the highest, he knows them.
roles: Depicts relatives sitting round the bed asking do you know me.
up_chhandogya.518.sa: पुरुषꣳ सोम्योतोपतापिनं ज्ञातयः पर्युपासते जानासि मां जानासि मामिति तस्य यावन्न वाङ्मनसि सम्पद्यते मनः प्राणे प्राणस्तेजसि तेजः परस्यां देवतायां तावज्जानाति ॥

up_chhandogya.521.m: They bring a man with his hands bound: 'He has stolen, he has committed theft; heat the axe for him.' If he did it, he makes himself false; covering himself with falsehood, he grasps the heated axe, is burned and is punished. If he did not do it, he makes himself true; covering himself with truth, he grasps the heated axe, is not burned and is released.
roles: Pictures truth as a covering that protects.
up_chhandogya.521.sa: पुरुषꣳ सोम्योत हस्तगृहीतमानयन्त्यपहार्षीत्स्तेयमकार्षीत्परशुमस्मै तपतेति स यदि तस्य कर्ता भवति तत एवानृतमात्मानं कुरुते सोऽनृताभिसंधोऽनृतेनात्मानमन्तर्धाय परशुं तप्तं प्रतिगृह्णाति स दह्यतेऽथ हन्यते ॥ अथ यदि तस्याकर्ता भवति ततेव सत्यमात्मानं कुरुते स सत्याभिसन्धः सत्येनात्मानमन्तर्धाय परशुं तप्तं प्रतिगृह्णाति सन दह्यतेऽथ मुच्यते ॥

scene.s: Uddalaka teaches his son through everyday experiments: a fast that dims the mind, a bird on a string, rivers merging in the sea, a banyan seed with nothing visible inside, salt dissolved in water, a blindfolded man finding his way home. Each lesson ends: 'That subtle essence is the self of all. You are that, Shvetaketu.'

up_chhandogya.526.m: 'Sir, I know only the texts; I do not know the self. I have heard from people like you that one who knows the self crosses beyond sorrow. I am in sorrow, sir. Please take me across.' He said to him: 'Whatever you have studied is only name.'
up_chhandogya.526.sa: सोऽहं भगवो मन्त्रविदेवास्मि नात्मविच्छ्रुतꣳ ह्येव मे भगवद्दृशेभ्यस्तरति शोकमात्मविदिति सोऽहं भगवः शोचामि तं मा भगवाञ्छोकस्य पारं तारयत्विति तꣳ होवाच यद्वै किंचैतदध्यगीष्ठा नामैवैतत् ॥

up_chhandogya.581.m: When one acts, one becomes steadfast. One does not become steadfast without acting; only by acting does one become steadfast. So action itself must be understood. 'Sir, I wish to understand action.'
roles: Shows steadiness is built by the doing itself.
up_chhandogya.581.sa: यदा वै करोत्यथ निस्तिष्ठति नाकृत्वा निस्तिष्ठति कृत्वैव निस्तिष्ठति कृतिस्त्वेव विजिज्ञासितव्येति कृतिं भगवो विजिज्ञास इति ॥

up_chhandogya.582.m: When one finds happiness, one acts. No one acts without finding happiness; only by finding happiness does one act. So happiness itself must be understood. 'Sir, I wish to understand happiness.'
roles: Ask what happiness the action is for.
up_chhandogya.582.sa: यदा वै सुखं लभतेऽथ करोति नासुखं लब्ध्वा करोति सुखमेव लब्ध्वा करोति सुखं त्वेव विजिज्ञासितव्यमिति सुखं भगवो विजिज्ञास इति ॥

up_chhandogya.583.m: The infinite alone is happiness; there is no happiness in the small. The infinite alone is happiness. So the infinite must be understood. 'Sir, I wish to understand the infinite.'
roles: Points happiness to what has no edge.
up_chhandogya.583.sa: यो वै भूमा तत्सुखं नाल्पे सुखमस्ति भूमैव सुखं भूमा त्वेव विजिज्ञासितव्य इति भूमानं भगवो विजिज्ञास इति ॥

up_chhandogya.585.m: Here people call cows and horses greatness, elephants and gold, servants and wives, fields and houses. I do not say so, I do not say so, for each of these rests on something else.
roles: Shows real greatness rests on nothing outside itself.
up_chhandogya.585.sa: गोअश्वमिह महिमेत्याचक्षते हस्तिहिरण्यं दासभार्यं क्षेत्राण्यायतनानीति नाहमेवं ब्रवीमि ब्रवीमीति होवाचान्योह्यन्यस्मिन्प्रतिष्ठित इति ॥

up_chhandogya.612.m: As people who do not know the spot walk again and again over a hidden treasure of gold buried in the ground and do not find it, so all these creatures go day after day into that world of Brahman and do not find it, for they are carried away by untruth.
roles: Shows the self in the heart visited nightly and going unrecognised.
up_chhandogya.612.sa: अनृतापिधानास्तद्यथापि हिरण्यनिधिं निहितमक्षेत्रज्ञा उपर्युपरि सञ्चरन्तो न विन्देयुरेवमेवेमाः सर्वाः प्रजा अहरहर्गच्छन्त्य एतं ब्रह्मलोकं न विन्दन्त्यनृतेन हि प्रत्यूढाः ॥

up_chhandogya.639.m: Virochana, content at heart, went to the asuras and taught them this teaching: 'The body alone is to be worshipped here, the body alone is to be tended. Worshipping the body and tending it, one wins both worlds, this one and the next.'
roles: Shows how a half-heard teaching becomes a creed of the body.
up_chhandogya.639.sa: विरोचनोऽसुराञ्जगाम तेभ्यो हैतामुपनिषदं प्रोवाचात्मैवेह महय्य आत्मा परिचर्य आत्मानमेवेह महयन्नात्मानं परिचरन्नुभौ लोकाववाप्नोतीमं चामुं चेति ॥

scene.s: Indra of the gods and Virochana of the demons study with Prajapati for 32 years to learn the self. Shown their dressed-up reflections, both leave satisfied; Virochana goes home teaching that the body is everything. Indra stops halfway, sees the flaw, and keeps coming back for 101 years until he learns that the self is not the body.

up_chhandogya.641.m: But Indra, before he reached the gods, saw this danger: 'Just as this self is well adorned when the body is well adorned, well dressed when it is well dressed, so it will be blind when the body is blind, lame when it is lame, crippled when it is crippled, and will perish when the body perishes. I see no good in this.'
up_chhandogya.641.sa: अथ हेन्द्रोऽप्राप्यैव देवानेतद्भयं ददर्श यथैव खल्वयमस्मिञ्छरीरे साध्वलंकृते साध्वलंकृतो भवति सुवसने सुवसनः परिष्कृते परिष्कृत एवमेवायमस्मिन्नन्धेऽन्धो भवति स्रामे स्रामः परिवृक्णे परिवृक्णोऽस्यैव शरीरस्य नाशमन्वेष नश्यति नाहमत्र भोग्यं पश्यामीति ॥

scene.s: Indra of the gods and Virochana of the demons study with Prajapati for 32 years to learn the self. Shown their dressed-up reflections, both leave satisfied; Virochana goes home teaching that the body is everything. Indra stops halfway, sees the flaw, and keeps coming back for 101 years until he learns that the self is not the body.

up_chhandogya.644.m: 'So it is, Maghavan,' he said. 'I will explain it to you further. Live here another thirty-two years.' He lived there another thirty-two years.
roles: Shows he stays, again and again, a hundred and one years in all.
up_chhandogya.644.sa: एवमेवैष मघवन्निति होवाचैतं त्वेव ते भूयोऽनुव्याख्यास्यामि वसापराणि द्वात्रिꣳशतं वर्षाणीति स हापराणि द्वात्रिꣳशतं वर्षाण्युवास तस्मै होवाच ॥

scene.s: Indra of the gods and Virochana of the demons study with Prajapati for 32 years to learn the self. Shown their dressed-up reflections, both leave satisfied; Virochana goes home teaching that the body is everything. Indra stops halfway, sees the flaw, and keeps coming back for 101 years until he learns that the self is not the body.

up_chhandogya.655.m: Maghavan, this body is mortal, held by death. It is the dwelling of the deathless, bodiless self. The embodied self is held by pleasure and pain; for one in the body there is no escape from pleasure and pain. But pleasure and pain do not touch one who is free of the body.
roles: You live in the body; you are not it.
up_chhandogya.655.sa: मघवन्मर्त्यं वा इदꣳ शरीरमात्तं मृत्युना तदस्यामृतस्याशरीरस्यात्मनोऽधिष्ठानमात्तो वै सशरीरः प्रियाप्रियाभ्यां न वै सशरीरस्य सतः प्रियाप्रिययोरपहतिरस्त्यशरीरं वाव सन्तं न प्रियाप्रिये स्पृशतः ॥

scene.s: Indra of the gods and Virochana of the demons study with Prajapati for 32 years to learn the self. Shown their dressed-up reflections, both leave satisfied; Virochana goes home teaching that the body is everything. Indra stops halfway, sees the flaw, and keeps coming back for 101 years until he learns that the self is not the body.

up_chhandogya.663.m: Brahma told this to Prajapati, Prajapati to Manu, Manu to the people. One who has studied the Veda in a teacher's house, doing the teacher's work in his spare time, returns home, lives as a householder in a clean place, keeps studying, raises virtuous children, draws all his senses into the self, and harms no living being except where sanctioned: living this way all his life, he reaches the world of Brahman and does not return.
roles: A whole life of steady, ordinary practice.
up_chhandogya.663.sa: तधैतद्ब्रह्मा प्रजापतयै उवाच प्रजापतिर्मनवे मनुः प्रजाभ्यः आचार्यकुलाद्वेदमधीत्य यथाविधानं गुरोः कर्मातिशेषेणाभिसमावृत्य कुटुम्बे शुचौ देशे स्वाध्यायमधीयानो धर्मिकान्विदधदात्मनि सर्वैन्द्रियाणि सम्प्रतिष्ठाप्याहिꣳसन्सर्व भूतान्यन्यत्र तीर्थेभ्यः स खल्वेवं वर्तयन्यावदायुषं ब्रह्मलोकमभिसम्पद्यते न च पुनरावर्तते न च पुनरावर्तते ॥

up_dakhsinamurti.26.m: In a vessel full of awakening, filled with the oil of detachment and fitted with the wick of devotion, behold the lamp of knowing. In the hollow darkness of delusion it rises of itself. Make detachment the lower fire-stick and knowledge the upper.
roles: Shows the light then rises of itself.
up_dakhsinamurti.26.sa: स होवाच । वैराग्यतैलसम्पूर्णे भक्तिवर्तिसमन्विते । प्रबोधपूर्णपात्रे तु ज्ञप्तिदीपं विलोकयेत् ॥ मोहान्धकारे निःसारे उदेति स्वयमेव हि । वैराग्यमरणिं कृत्वा ज्ञानं कृत्वोत्तरारणिम् ॥

up_devi.15.m: She is the power of the Self. She enchants the world, holding noose, goad, bow and arrow. She is the great wisdom. Whoever knows this crosses beyond grief.
roles: She is the power of one's own self.
up_devi.15.sa: एषात्मशक्तिः । एषा विश्वमोहिनी पाशाङ्कुशधनुर्बाणधरा । एषा श्रीमहाविद्या । य एवं वेद स शोकं तरति ।

up_devi.16.m: Salutations to you, Blessed One. Mother, protect us on every side. She is the eight Vasus; she is the eleven Rudras; she is the twelve Adityas.
up_devi.16.sa: नमस्ते अस्तु भगवति भवति मातरस्मान्पातु सर्वतः । सैषाष्टौ वसवः । सैषैकादश रुद्राः। सैषा द्वादशादित्याः ।

up_devi.19.m: I bow to her always: the Goddess who takes away pain, giver of both enjoyment and freedom, endless, victorious, pure, the refuge, the giver of good, the kind one.
roles: She is called sharanya, fit to be taken refuge in.
up_devi.19.sa: तामहं प्रणौमि नित्यम् । तापापहारिणीं देवीं भुक्तिमुक्तिप्रदायिनीम् । अनन्तां विजयां शुद्धां शरण्यां शिवदां शिवाम् ॥

up_devi.25.m: I bow to you, Goddess, destroyer of great fear, who calms great hardship, whose very form is great compassion.
roles: Courage borrowed from the one bowed to.
up_devi.25.sa: नमामि त्वामहं देवीं महाभयविनाशिनीम् । महादुर्गप्रशमनीं महाकारुण्यरूपिणीम् ॥

up_devi.29.m: There is nothing higher than her; she is called Durga. Because she rescues from hardship, the Goddess is called Durga.
roles: Shows strength to keep walking the hard stretch.
up_devi.29.sa: यस्याः परतरं नास्ति सैषा दुर्गा प्रकीर्तिता । दुर्गात्संत्रायते यस्माद्देवी दुर्गेति कथ्यते ॥

up_devi.30.m: To that Durga, hard to reach, the Goddess who destroys wrongdoing, who carries us across the ocean of worldly life: afraid of that life, I bow.
roles: Shows fear turned into a bow.
up_devi.30.sa: तां दुर्गां दुर्गमां देवीं दुराचारविघातिनीम् । नमामि भवभीतोऽहं संसारार्णवतारिणीम् ॥

up_devi.9.m: She who is fire-coloured, blazing with austerity, radiant, sought by those who act: in Durga, the Goddess, I take refuge. She utterly destroys the darkness.
up_devi.9.sa: तामग्निवर्णां तपसा ज्वलन्तीं वैरोचनीं कर्मफलेषु जुष्टाम् । दुर्गां देवीं शरणमहं प्रपद्ये सुतरां नाशयते तमः ॥

up_isha.1.m: All of this, whatever moves in this moving world, is pervaded by the Lord. Enjoy it by letting go. Do not covet; whose is wealth, after all?
roles: Shows what you have is seen as held in trust.
up_isha.1.sa: ॐ ईशा वास्यमिदꣳ सर्वं यत्किञ्च जगत्यां जगत् । तेन त्यक्तेन भुञ्जीथा मा गृधः कस्यस्विद्धनम् ॥

up_isha.15.m: The face of truth is covered by a golden vessel. Uncover it, O Pushan, so that I, who hold to truth, may see.
roles: Asks for seeing and does not seize it.
up_isha.15.sa: हिरण्मयेन पात्रेण सत्यस्यापिहितं मुखम् । तत्त्वं पूषन्नपावृणु सत्यधर्माय दृष्टये ॥

up_isha.18.m: O Agni, lead us by the good path to true wealth, O god who knows all our ways. Keep crooked wrongdoing away from us. We offer you our fullest words of reverence.
roles: Shows the one who knows all our ways being asked to lead.
up_isha.18.sa: अग्ने नय सुपथा राये अस्मान् विश्वानि देव वयुनानि विद्वान् । युयोध्यस्मज्जुहुराणमेनो भूयिष्ठां ते नमौक्तिं विधेम ॥

up_isha.2.m: Doing your work here, you may wish to live a hundred years. For you there is no other way than this: done in this spirit, action does not cling to a person.
roles: A lifelong steady way of working.
up_isha.2.sa: कुर्वन्नेवेह कर्माणि जिजीविषेच्छतꣳ समाः । एवं त्वयि नान्यथेतोऽस्ति न कर्म लिप्यते नरे ॥

up_isha.6.m: One who sees all beings in the self, and the self in all beings, no longer shrinks away from anyone.
roles: Shows the self as what is shared by all beings.
up_isha.6.sa: यस्तु सर्वाणि भूतान्यात्मन्येवानुपश्यति । सर्वभूतेषु चात्मानं ततो न विजुगुप्सते ॥

up_isha.7.m: For the one who knows, in whom all beings have become the self, what confusion, what sorrow can there be, seeing oneness everywhere?
roles: All beings have become the self for the one who knows.
up_isha.7.sa: यस्मिन्सर्वाणि भूतान्यात्मैवाभूद्विजानतः । तत्र को मोहः कः शोक एकत्वमनुपश्यतः ॥

up_kath.1.1.11.m: Your father, Auddalaki Aruni, will know you as before, by my leave. He will sleep peacefully at night, his anger gone, when he sees you released from the jaws of death.
roles: Names the son's first wish for his father's peace.

scene.s: Death, away from home, keeps the boy waiting three days and offers three boons in apology. Nachiketa asks first that his father be calm and not angry with him, then for a sacred fire, then for the truth about death. Yama tempts him with sons, gold, long life and pleasures instead; the boy refuses them all.
scene.t: The three boons and the refused fortune

up_kath.1.1.4.m: He said to his father, 'Father, to whom will you give me?' He asked a second time, and a third. His father said, 'To Death I give you.'
roles: Speaks a parent's worst sentence in a flash of temper.
up_kath.1.1.4.sa: स होवाच पितर तत कस्मै मां दास्यसीति। द्वितीयं तृतीयं तꣳहोवाच मृत्युवे वा ददामीति ॥

scene.s: A father makes a show of giving away all he owns, but the cows are old and dry. His young son Nachiketa keeps asking who he will be given to, until the father snaps, 'To Death!' The boy goes, and tells his father to keep his word.

up_kath.1.1.5.m: Among many I go first; among many I go in the middle. What can Yama have to do that he will do with me today?
roles: Shows him walking toward death without panic.
up_kath.1.1.5.sa: बहूनामेमि प्रथमो बहूनामेमि मध्यमः । किꣳस्त्रिद्यमस्य कर्तव्यं यन्मयाद्य करिष्यति ॥

scene.s: A father makes a show of giving away all he owns, but the cows are old and dry. His young son Nachiketa keeps asking who he will be given to, until the father snaps, 'To Death!' The boy goes, and tells his father to keep his word.

up_kath.1.1.6.m: Look back at how those before us fared; look ahead at how those after us will fare. Like grain a mortal ripens, and like grain is born again.
roles: Keeping one's word matters more than keeping one's comfort.
up_kath.1.1.6.sa: अनुपश्य यथा पूर्वे प्रतिपश्य यथा परे । सस्यमिव मत्यैः पच्यते सस्यमिवाजायते पुनः ॥

scene.s: A father makes a show of giving away all he owns, but the cows are old and dry. His young son Nachiketa keeps asking who he will be given to, until the father snaps, 'To Death!' The boy goes, and tells his father to keep his word.

up_kath.1.2.2.m: The good and the pleasant both come to a person. The wise one examines them and tells them apart. The wise chooses the good over the pleasant; the dull chooses the pleasant, for getting and keeping.
roles: Shows examining the two closely and telling them apart.
up_kath.1.2.2.sa: श्रेयश्च प्रेयश्च मनुष्यमेतस्तौ सम्परीत्य विविनक्ति धीर:। श्रेयो हि धीरोऽभि प्रेयसो वृणीते प्रेयो मन्दो योगक्षेमाद् वृणीते ॥

up_kath.1.2.22.m: Knowing the self as bodiless within bodies, steady among the unsteady, great and all-pervading, the wise one does not grieve.
roles: Shows the self as the stable one among all that shifts.
up_kath.1.2.22.sa: अशरीरँ शरीरेष्वनवस्थेष्ववस्थितम् । महान्तं विभुमात्मानं मत्वा धीरो न शोचति ॥

up_kath.1.2.23.m: This self is not reached by lectures, nor by intellect, nor by much learning. It is reached by the one it chooses; to that one the self reveals its own form.
roles: Shows what counts is wanting the self itself.
up_kath.1.2.23.sa: नायमात्मा प्रवचनेन लभ्यो न मेधया न बहुना श्रुतेन । यमेवैष वृणुते तेन लभ्यः तस्यैष आत्मा विवृणुते तनूꣳ स्वाम् ॥

up_kath.1.2.24.m: One who has not turned away from wrong conduct, who is not calm, not collected, whose mind is not at peace, cannot reach it by cleverness alone.
roles: Shows a quiet, collected mind is the precondition.
up_kath.1.2.24.sa: नाविरतो दुश्चरितामाशान्तो ना समाहितः । नाशान्त मानसो वापि प्रज्ञानेनैनमाप्नुयात् ॥

up_kath.1.3.14.m: Arise! Awake! Go to the great ones and learn. Sharp as a razor's edge, hard to cross, is that path, say the wise.
roles: Shows going to those who know and learning.
up_kath.1.3.14.sa: उत्तिष्ठत जाग्रत प्राप्य वरान्निबोधत । क्षुरस्य धारा निशिता दुरत्यया दुर्गं पथस्तत्कवयो वदन्ति ॥

up_kath.1.3.3.m: Know the self as the rider, the body as the chariot, the intellect as the charioteer and the mind as the reins. The senses, they say, are the horses, and the things of the world are the roads they run on.
roles: Shows you are the one carried, not the vehicle or the horses.
up_kath.1.3.3.sa: आत्मानँ रथितं विद्धि शरीरँ रथमेव तु । बुद्धिं तु सारथिं विद्धि मनः प्रग्रहमेव च ॥ इन्द्रियाणि हयानाहुर्विषयांस्तेषु गोचरान् । आत्मेन्द्रिय मनोयुक्त भोक्तेत्याहुर्मनीषिणः ॥

up_kath.1.3.5.m: For one who lacks understanding, whose mind is never held steady, the senses run out of control like a driver's wild horses. For one who has understanding, whose mind is always steady, the senses obey like good horses.
up_kath.1.3.5.sa: यस्त्वविज्ञानवान्भवत्ययुक्तेन मनसा सदा । तस्येन्द्रियाण्यवश्यानि दुष्टाश्वा इव सारथेः ॥ यस्तु विज्ञानवान्भवति युक्तेन मनसा सदा । तस्येन्द्रियाणि वश्यानि सदश्वा इव सारथेः ॥

up_kath.2.1.1.m: The self-existent one made the senses face outward, so a person looks outward, not within. A rare wise one, seeking the deathless, turned the gaze inward and saw the self.
roles: Shows the self is found by turning the gaze around.
up_kath.2.1.1.sa: पराञ्चि खानि व्यतृणत् स्वयम्भूस्तस्मात्पराङ्पश्यति नान्तरात्मन्। कश्चिद्धीरः प्रत्यगात्मानमैक्षदावृत्तचक्षुरमृतत्वमिच्छन् ॥

up_kath.2.1.2.m: The immature chase outward pleasures and walk into the wide-spread net of death. The wise, knowing what is deathless, do not look for the lasting among things that pass.
roles: Stop asking permanence of impermanent things.
up_kath.2.1.2.sa: पराचः कामाननुयन्ति बालास्ते मृत्योर्यन्ति विततस्य पाशम् । अथ धीरा अमृतत्वं विदित्वा ध्रुवमध्रुवेष्विह न प्रार्थयन्ते ॥

up_kath.2.2.11.m: Just as the sun, the eye of the whole world, is not stained by the flaws the eyes see outside, so the one inner self of all beings is not stained by the sorrow of the world; it stands apart.
roles: Shows the inner self illumining everything and being touched by none of it.
up_kath.2.2.11.sa: सूर्यो यथा सर्वलोकस्य चक्षुः न लिप्यते चाक्षुषैर्बाह्यदोषैः । एकस्तथा सर्वभूतान्तरात्मा न लिप्यते लोकदुःखेन बाह्यः ॥

up_kath.2.2.15.m: There the sun does not shine, nor the moon and stars; these lightnings do not shine, much less this fire. When that shines, everything shines after it; by its light all this is lit.
roles: Shows the mind resting on the source of all brightness.
up_kath.2.2.15.sa: न तत्र सूर्यो भाति न चन्द्रतारकं नेमा विद्युतो भान्ति कुतोऽयमग्निः । तमेव भान्तमनुभाति सर्वं तस्य भासा सर्वमिदं विभाति ॥

up_kath.2.3.15.m: When all the knots of the heart are cut, here in this life, the mortal becomes immortal. This much is the whole teaching.
roles: Shows freedom placed in this life.
up_kath.2.3.15.sa: यदा सर्वे प्रभिद्यन्ते हृदयस्येह ग्रन्थयः । अथ मर्त्योऽमृतो भवत्येतावद्ध्यनुशासनम् ॥

up_katharudra.17.m: Let him not torment the body too much for the sake of pleasure or pain. Praised, let him not gloat; blamed, let him not curse others.
roles: Shows holding back the harsh word when criticised.
up_katharudra.17.sa: नात्यर्थं सुखदुःखाभ्यां शरीरमुपतायेत् । स्तूयमानो न तुषेत निन्दितो न शपेत्परान् ॥

up_kaushitaki.126.m: Without attention, speech conveys no word at all. A person says, 'My mind was elsewhere; I did not catch that word.' Without attention, breath conveys no smell. A person says, 'My mind was elsewhere; I did not notice that smell.'
roles: Shows my mind was elsewhere, I did not catch that.
up_kaushitaki.126.sa: न हि प्रज्ञापेता वाङ्नाम किंचन प्रज्ञपयेदन्यत्र मे मनोऽभूदित्याह नाहमेतन्नाम प्राज्ञासिषमिति न हि प्रज्ञापेतः प्राणो गन्धं कंचन प्रज्ञपयेदन्यत्र मे मनोऽभूदित्याह नाहमेतं गन्धं प्राज्ञासिषमिति नहि

up_kaushitaki.131.m: One should not seek to know speech; one should know the speaker. Not smell, but the one who smells; not form, but the one who sees it; not sound, but the hearer; not taste, but the one who tastes. Not action, but the doer; not pleasure and pain, but the one who knows pleasure and pain; not delight, but its knower; not movement, but the mover.
roles: Knows the one who knows pleasure and pain.
up_kaushitaki.131.sa: न वाचं विजिज्ञासीत वक्तारं विद्यान्न गन्धं विजिज्ञासीत घ्रातारं विद्यान्न रूपं विजिज्ञासीत रूपविदं विद्यान्न शब्दं विजिज्ञासीत श्रोतारं विद्यान्नान्नरसं विजिज्ञासीतान्नरसविज्ञातारं विद्यान्न कर्म विजिज्ञासीत कर्तारं विद्यान्न सुखदुःखे विजिज्ञासीत सुखदुःखयोर्विज्ञातारं विद्यान्नानन्दं रतिं प्रजातिं विजिज्ञासीतानन्दस्य रतेः प्रजातेर्विज्ञातारं विद्यान्नेत्यां विजिज्ञासीतैतारं विद्यान्न

up_kaushitaki.3.m: He said, 'I do not know this. Let me ask my teacher.' He went to his father and asked. The father said, 'I too do not know it. We have studied the Veda and take what others give us. Come, let us both go.'
roles: Shows father and son becoming students together.
up_kaushitaki.3.sa: स होवाच नाहमेतद्वेद हन्ताचार्यं प्रच्छानीति स ह पितरमासाद्य पप्रच्छेतीति स होवाचाहमप्येतन्न वेद सदस्येव वयं स्वाध्यायमधीत्य हरामहे यन्नः परे ददत्येह्युभौ गमिष्याव इति ॥

scene.s: A patron asks young Shvetaketu a question he cannot answer. He asks his father, who admits he does not know either and suggests they both go to the patron as students. Chitra welcomes Uddalaka for his humility.
scene.t: Father and son go back to school

up_kaushitaki.93.m: 'I place my joys and sorrows in you,' says the father. 'I take your joys and sorrows into me,' says the son. 'I place my pleasure, delight and power of begetting in you,' says the father. 'I take them into me,' says the son. 'I place my going in you,' says the father. 'I take your going into me,' says the son.
roles: Shows the child saying I take it to everything given.
up_kaushitaki.93.sa: सुखदुःखे मे त्वयि दधानीति पिता सुखदुःखे ते मयि दध इति पुत्र आनन्दं रतिं प्रजाइं मे त्वयि दधानीति पिता आनन्दं रतिं प्रजातिं ते मयि दध इति पुत्र इत्यां मे त्वयि दधानीति पिता इत्यां ते मयि दध इति पुत्रो

scene.s: When a father feels death near, he lies down and his son lies over him, and they exchange words: the father places his speech, breath, sight, hearing, joys and sorrows in the son, and the son receives each one.

up_kaushitaki.93.sp: A dying father and his son

up_maha.104.m: Trees also live; animals and birds also live. That person truly lives whose mind lives by reflection.
roles: Reflection is what makes a life human.
up_maha.104.sa: तरवोऽपि हि जीवन्ति जीवन्ति मृगपक्षिणः । स जीवति मनो यस्य मननेनोपजीवति ॥

up_maha.106.m: Scripture is a burden to the undiscerning, knowledge a burden to the passionate, the mind a burden to the restless, the body a burden to one who does not know the self.
roles: Shows the mind is a burden to the one who is not at peace.
up_maha.106.sa: भारो विवेकिनः शास्त्रं भारो ज्ञानं च रागिणः । अशान्तस्य मनो भारो भारोऽनात्मविदो वपुः ॥

up_maha.107.m: From ego come misfortunes; from ego come troubles of the mind; from ego come cravings. There is no enemy greater than ego.
roles: Names looking for the 'I' behind the upset.

up_maha.109.m: The mind runs here and there, restless and pointless; it wanders far away, like a dog in a village.
roles: A seeker describes his own mind running everywhere for nothing.
up_maha.109.sa: इतश्चेतश्च सुव्यग्रं व्यर्थमेवाभिधावति । मनो दूरतरं याति ग्रामे कौलेयको यथा ॥

up_maha.111.m: Harder than drinking up the ocean, harder than uprooting Mount Meru, harder even than swallowing fire, is the mastery of the mind.
roles: Depicts the speaker finding his mind harder than any feat.

up_maha.113.m: Whatever good quality I take refuge in, great sage, craving cuts it away, as a mouse gnaws through a string.
roles: Depicts the discouragement of watching good intentions cut.
up_maha.113.sa: यां यामहं मुनिश्रेष्ठ संश्रयामि गुणश्रियम् । तां तां कृन्तति मे तृष्णा तन्त्रीमिव कुमूषिका ॥

up_maha.114.m: It sets foot even where no one can go; even when satisfied it strives in vain; it never stays long in one place: craving is a restless monkey.
roles: Shows never long in one place.
up_maha.114.sa: पदं करोत्यलङ्घ्येऽपि तृप्ता विफलमीहते । चिरं तिष्ठति नैकत्र तृष्णा चपलमर्कटी ॥

up_maha.144.m: Misfortunes come in a moment; good fortune comes in a moment; birth in a moment, then death. All of it is passing.
roles: Shows the same clock running on good and bad times.
up_maha.144.sa: आपदः क्षणमायान्ति क्षणमायान्ति सम्पदः । क्षणं जन्माथ मरणं सर्वं नश्वरमेव तत् ॥

up_maha.150.m: Four gatekeepers are named at the door of freedom: calm, inquiry, contentment, and the company of good people. Take refuge in even one of them with full effort, setting all else aside; when one is won, all four come under your control.
roles: Contentment is named as a door, not a reward.
up_maha.150.sa: मोक्षद्वारे द्वारपालश्चत्वारः परिकीर्तिताः । शमो विचारः सन्तोषश्चतुर्थः साधुसङ्गमः ॥ एकं वा सर्वयत्नेन सर्वमुत्सृज्य संश्रयेत् । एकस्मिन्वशगे यान्ति चत्वारोऽपि वशं गताः ॥

up_maha.165.m: In adversity they do not wilt, as the golden lotus does not close at night. They want nothing beyond what is at hand and delight in the path of the good.
roles: Shows staying open in the dark like the golden lotus at night.
up_maha.165.sa: नापदि ग्लानिमायान्ति निशि हेमाम्बुजं यथा । नेहन्ते प्रकृतादन्यद्रमन्ते शिष्टवर्त्मनि ॥

up_maha.178.m: Whatever sorrows, whatever craving, whatever unbearable anxieties there are, all of them vanish in calm minds, as darkness vanishes before the sun.
roles: Gives a reason to value calm above fixing each worry.
up_maha.178.sa: यानि दुःखानि या तृष्णा दुःसहा ये दुराधयः । शान्तचेतःसु तत्सर्वं तमोऽर्केष्विव नश्यति ॥

up_maha.179.m: All beings, the harsh and the gentle alike, come to trust the person who is calm, as they would trust a mother.
roles: Shows trust grows around the one who does not react.
up_maha.179.sa: मातरीव परं यान्ति विषमाणि मृदूनि च । विश्वासमिह भूतानि सर्वाणि शमशालिनि ॥

up_maha.180.m: Not by drinking elixirs, not by the embrace of Lakshmi, does a person find such happiness as by calm within.
roles: Shows happiness is placed within reach, inside.
up_maha.180.sa: न रसायनपानेन न लक्ष्म्यालिङ्गितेन च । न तथा सुखमाप्नोति शमेनान्तर्यथा जनः ॥

up_maha.185.m: One who lets go of what has not come, stays even with what has come, and is untouched by gain or loss is called content. One who does not long for what is not attained, and enjoys what has come as it comes, gentle in conduct, is called content.
up_maha.185.sa: अप्राप्तं हि परित्यज्य सम्प्राप्ते समतां गतः । अदृष्टखेदाखेदो यः सन्तुष्ट इति कथ्यते ॥ नाभिनन्दत्यसम्प्राप्तं प्राप्तं भुङ्क्ते यथेप्सितम् । यः स सौम्यसमाचारः सन्तुष्ट इति कथ्यते ॥

up_maha.221.m: 'I am Brahman': this conviction is the cause of freedom for great souls. Two words bring bondage and freedom: 'mine' and 'not mine'. With 'mine' a creature is bound; with 'not mine' it is freed.
roles: Names 'I am Brahman' as the cause of freedom.
up_maha.221.sa: अहं ब्रह्मेति नियतं मोक्षहेतुर्महात्मनाम् । द्वे पदे बन्धमोक्षाय निर्ममेति ममेति च । ममेति बध्यते जन्तुर्निर्ममेति विमुच्यते ॥

up_maha.248.m: A mind without restlessness is nowhere to be seen. Restlessness is the nature of the mind, as heat is the nature of fire.
roles: Names it as nature takes away the fight with it.
up_maha.248.sa: न हि चञ्चलताहीनं मनः क्वचन दृश्यते । चञ्चलत्वं मनोधर्मो वह्नेर्धर्मो यथोष्णता ॥

up_maha.255.m: For those seized by the crocodile of craving and falling into the ocean of worldly life, swept along by its whirlpools, one's own mind is the boat. Cutting with the mind the mind's noose, the strongest of bonds, lift yourself across; no one else can carry you over.
up_maha.255.sa: तृष्णाग्राहगृहीतानां संसारार्णवपातिनाम् । आवर्तैरूह्यमानानां दूरं स्वमन एव नौः ॥ मनसैव मनश्छित्त्वा पाशं परमबन्धनम् । भवादुत्तारयात्मानं नासावन्येन तार्यते ॥

up_maha.260.m: Non-clinging alone is freedom; clinging is sorrow.
roles: Defines freedom as an open hand.

up_maha.369.m: However brave, however learned, however well born, however great, a person is bound by craving, as a lion is bound by a chain.
roles: Shows being caught by craving happens to the strongest.
up_maha.369.sa: धीरोऽप्यतिबहुज्ञोऽपि कुलजोऽपि महानपि । तृष्णया बध्यते जन्तुः सिंहः श‍ृङ्खलया यथा ॥

up_maha.370.m: Taking up supreme effort and steady striving, acting according to sound guidance and without anxiety, who would not succeed?
roles: Backs the decision to begin and keep going.
up_maha.370.sa: परमं पौरुषं यत्नमास्थादाय सृद्यमम् । यथाशास्त्रमनुद्वेगमाचरन्को न सिद्धिभाक् ॥

up_maha.40.m: Those pleasures and those foods did not move the mind of Vyasa's son, as a gentle breeze cannot move a mountain on its base. Only even, clear, silent and glad of heart, complete like the full moon, pure Shuka remained.
roles: Shows a mountain in a light breeze.
up_maha.40.sa: ते भोगास्तानि भोज्यानि व्यासपुत्रस्य तन्मनः । नाजह्वुर्मन्दपवनो बद्धपीठमिवाचलम् ॥ केवलं सुसमः स्वच्छो मौनी मुदितमानसः । सम्पूर्ण इव शीतांशुरतिष्ठदमलः शुकः ॥

scene.s: Young Shuka, already wise, is sent by his father Vyasa to King Janaka. Janaka ignores him at the gate for seven days, then lets him wait in the courtyard seven more, then surrounds him with luxury for seven days. Shuka stays exactly the same throughout, and Janaka bows to him.

up_maha.452.m: So, Nidagha, knower of truth, in the dealings of worldly life, let go of whatever is lost, and take up whatever comes.
roles: Shows loss and gain getting the same light hand.
up_maha.452.sa: अतो निदाघ तत्त्वज्ञ व्यवहारेषु संसृतेः । नष्टं नष्टमुपेक्षस्व प्राप्तं प्राप्तमुपाहर ॥

up_maha.453.m: Not longing for pleasures yet to come, and enjoying those that have come: this, unforced, is the mark of the wise.
roles: Shows enjoying what is here without effort or show.
up_maha.453.sa: अनागतानां भोगानामवाञ्छनमकृत्रिमम् । आगतानां च संभोग इति पण्डितलक्षणम् ॥

up_maha.467.m: As the husk of rice and the tarnish of copper are removed by work, so is a person's impurity. A person's impurity, like the husk on rice, may be natural, yet it surely goes; there is no doubt. So be industrious.
up_maha.467.sa: तण्डुलस्य यथा चर्म यथा ताम्रस्य कालिमा । नश्यति क्रियया विप्र पुरुषस्य तथा मलम् ॥ जीवस्य तण्डुलस्येव मलं सहजमप्यलम् । नश्यत्येव न सन्देहस्तस्मादुद्योगवान्भवेत् ॥

up_maha.532.m: Always doing the work that comes, seeing friend and foe alike, free of wanting and not-wanting, such a one neither grieves nor craves. Saying what is agreeable to all, speaking gently when asked, knowing the intent of others' hearts, such a one does not sink in the world.
roles: Speaks what is agreeable and gently, and understands what others intend.
up_maha.532.sa: प्राप्तकर्मकरो नित्यं शत्रुमित्रसमानदृक् । ईहितानीहितैर्मुक्तो न शोचति न काङ्क्षति ॥ सर्वस्याभिमतं वक्ता चोदितः पेशलोक्तिमान् । आशयज्ञश्च भूतानां संसारे नावसीदति ॥

up_maha.536.m: Outwardly busy, inwardly free of agitation; a doer on the outside, a non-doer within: move through the world with a clear mind.
roles: Shows acting fully without the inner heat.
up_maha.536.sa: बहिःकृत्रिमसंरंभो हृदि संरम्भवर्जितः । कर्ता बहिरकर्तान्तर्लोके विहर शुद्धधीः ॥

up_maha.539.m: 'This one is my own, that one is not': this is how the small-minded reckon. For those of generous character, the whole earth is one family.
roles: A large heart is defined by whom it includes.
up_maha.539.sa: अयं बन्धुरयं नेति गणना लघुचेतसाम् । उदारचरितानां तु वसुधैव कुटुम्बकम् ॥

up_maitrayani.13.m: In such a world, what use is the enjoyment of desires, when one who feeds on them is seen to return here again and again? Please lift me out. In this world I am like a frog in a dark well. Sir, you are my way, you are my way.
roles: Shows a person with everything asking what use any of it is.
up_maitrayani.13.sa: सोऽहमित्येतद्विधेऽस्मिन्संसारे किं कामोपभोगैर्यैरेवाश्रितस्यासकृदिहावर्तनं दृश्यत इत्युद्धर्तुमर्हसीत्यन्धोदपानस्थो भेक इवाहमस्मिन्संसारे भगवंस्त्वं नो गतिस्त्वं नो गतिः ॥

up_maitrayani.78.m: The mind itself is the world we wander in; so purify it with effort. What one's mind dwells on, that one becomes. This is the ancient secret.
roles: Shows cleaning the mind is named as work worth effort.
up_maitrayani.78.sa: चित्तमेव हि संसारस्तत्प्रयत्नेन शोधयेत् । यच्चित्तस्तन्मयो भवति गुह्यमेतत्सनातनम् ॥

up_maitrayani.8.m: We see that all this perishes, like gnats and mosquitoes, like grass and trees that spring up and wither.
