roles: A king looks at everything and sees only that it ends.
up_maitrayani.8.sa: सर्वं चेदं क्षयिष्णु पश्यामो यथेमे दंशमशकादयस्तृणवन्नश्यतयोद्भूतप्रध्वंसिनः ॥

scene.s: A king hands his throne to his son and goes to the forest, overwhelmed by how everything decays. When a sage offers him a wish, he says he feels like a frog in a dark well and asks to be shown the way out.

up_maitrayani.80.m: If a person's mind were as attached to Brahman as it is attached to the objects of the senses, who would not be freed from bondage?
roles: Shows one already has the strength of attachment the path needs.
up_maitrayani.80.sa: समासक्तं यदा चित्तं जन्तोर्विषयगोचरे । यद्येवं ब्रह्मणि स्यात्तत्को न मुच्येत बन्धनात् ॥

up_maitrayani.86.m: The mind alone is the cause of bondage and of liberation for human beings: attached to objects, it binds; free of objects, it liberates.
roles: Shows freedom as the mind unhooked.
up_maitrayani.86.sa: मन एव मनुष्याणां कारणं बन्धमोक्षयोः । बन्धाय विषयासक्तं मुक्त्यै निर्विषयं स्मृतमिति ॥

up_maitreya.24.m: Mahadeva said: The body is called a temple; the living being in it is Shiva alone. Cast off ignorance like yesterday's flower offerings, and worship with the sense 'I am He.'
roles: Shows worship as identity I am He.
up_maitreya.24.sa: स होवाच महादेवः ॥ देहो देवालयः प्रोक्तः स जीवः केवलः शिवः । त्यजेदज्ञाननिर्माल्यं सोऽहम्भावेन पूजयेत् ॥

up_maitreya.25.m: Seeing no difference is knowledge; a mind free of objects is meditation; giving up the mind's dirt is bathing; restraint of the senses is purity.
roles: Meditation is a mind at rest from objects.
up_maitreya.25.sa: अभेददर्शनं ज्ञानं ध्यानं निर्विषयं मनः। स्नानं मनोमलत्यागः शौचमिन्द्रियनिग्रहः ॥

up_mundaka.1.1.3.m: Shaunaka, the great householder, approached Angiras in the proper way and asked: 'Sir, what is that which, when known, makes all this known?'
roles: Shows a man with a great household coming with one question.
up_mundaka.1.1.3.sa: शौनको ह वै महाशालोऽङ्गिरसं विधिवदुपसन्नः पप्रच्छ । कस्मिन्नु भगवो विज्ञाते सर्वमिदं विज्ञातं भवतीति ॥

up_mundaka.1.1.4.m: He said: two kinds of knowledge are to be known, so the knowers of Brahman say: the higher and the lower. The lower is the four Vedas, phonetics, ritual, grammar, etymology, metre and astronomy. The higher is that by which the imperishable is reached.
roles: Shows opening the question of what the higher knowing is.
up_mundaka.1.1.4.sa: तस्मै स होवाच । द्वे विद्ये वेदितव्ये इति ह स्मयद्ब्रह्मविदो वदन्ति परा चैवापरा च॥ तत्रापरा ऋग्वेदो यजुर्वेदः सामवेदोऽथर्ववेदः शिक्षा कल्पो व्याकरणं निरुक्तं छन्दो ज्योतिषमिति । अथ परा यया तदक्षरमधिगम्यते ॥

up_mundaka.1.2.12.m: Having examined the worlds won by work, a seeker should grow dispassionate: what is not made cannot be gained by what is made. To know it, let him go, fuel in hand, to a teacher who is learned and rooted in Brahman.
roles: Goes and asks someone who knows.
up_mundaka.1.2.12.sa: परीक्ष्य लोकान् कर्मचितान् ब्राह्मणो निर्वेदमायान्नास्त्यकृतः कृतेन । तद्विज्ञानार्थं स गुरुमेवाभिगच्छेत् समित्पाणिः श्रोत्रियं ब्रह्मनिष्ठम् ॥

up_mundaka.1.2.8.m: Living in ignorance, wise in their own eyes, thinking themselves learned, the deluded go round and round, stumbling, like the blind led by the blind.
roles: Shows checking whether one's guide can see.
up_mundaka.1.2.8.sa: अविद्यायामन्तरे वर्तमानाः स्वयं धीराः पण्डितं मन्यमानाः । जङ्घन्यमानाः परियन्ति मूढा अन्धेनैव नीयमाना यथान्धाः ॥

up_mundaka.2.2.4.m: Om is the bow, the self is the arrow, and Brahman is called the target. It must be hit by one who is undistracted; like the arrow, one becomes one with it.
roles: Sends the self into Brahman like an arrow into its mark.
up_mundaka.2.2.4.sa: प्रणवो धनुः शारो ह्यात्मा ब्रह्म तल्लक्ष्यमुच्यते । अप्रमत्तेन वेद्धव्यं शरवत् तन्मयो भवेत् ॥

up_mundaka.2.2.8.m: The knot of the heart is cut, all doubts are dispelled and one's deeds wear away, when that which is both high and low is seen.
roles: Shows seeing that which is both cause and effect.
up_mundaka.2.2.8.sa: भिद्यते हृदयग्रन्थिश्छिद्यन्ते सर्वसंशयाः । क्षीयन्ते चास्य कर्माणि तस्मिन् दृष्टे परावरे ॥

up_mundaka.3.1.1.m: Two birds, inseparable companions, cling to the same tree. One of them eats the sweet fruit; the other, not eating, simply watches.
roles: Shows the witness as one's closest companion on the same tree.
up_mundaka.3.1.1.sa: द्वा सुपर्णा सयुजा सखाया समानं वृक्षं परिषस्वजाते । तयोरन्यः पिप्पलं स्वाद्वत्त्यनश्नन्नन्यो अभिचाकशीति ॥

up_mundaka.3.1.2.m: On the same tree a person sits sunk, grieving, bewildered by his own helplessness. When he sees the other, the content lord, and his greatness, his sorrow leaves him.
roles: Shows turn and see the one who watches.
up_mundaka.3.1.2.sa: समाने वृक्षे पुरुषो निमग्नोऽनिशया शोचति मुह्यमानः । जुष्टं यदा पश्यत्यन्यमीशमस्य महिमानमिति वीतशोकः ॥

up_mundaka.3.1.4.m: This is the life that shines through all beings. Knowing it, the wise one does not talk over others. Delighting in the self, playing in the self, yet active, such a one is the best of the knowers of Brahman.
roles: Plays and delights in the self.
up_mundaka.3.1.4.sa: प्रणो ह्येष यः सर्वभूतैर्विभाति विजानन् विद्वान् भवते नातिवादी । आत्मक्रीड आत्मरतिः क्रियावानेष ब्रह्मविदां वरिष्ठः ॥

up_mundaka.3.1.6.m: Truth alone wins, not falsehood. By truth the divine path is laid out, by which the sages, their desires fulfilled, travel to where the highest treasure of truth is.
roles: Shows truth wins over time, so one can hold.
up_mundaka.3.1.6.sa: सत्यमेव जयते नानृतं सत्येन पन्था विततो देवयानः । येनाऽऽक्रमन्त्यृषयो ह्याप्तकामा यत्र तत् सत्यस्य परमं निधानम् ॥

up_mundaka.3.2.2.m: One who desires, brooding on desires, is born here and there by those desires. But for one whose desire is fulfilled, who is whole in himself, all desires dissolve right here.
roles: Shows desires going quiet within wholeness.
up_mundaka.3.2.2.sa: कामान् यः कामयते मन्यमानः स कामभिर्जायते तत्र तत्र । पर्याप्तकामस्य कृतात्मनस्तु इहैव सर्वे प्रविलीयन्ति कामाः ॥

up_mundaka.3.2.4.m: This self is not won by the weak, nor through carelessness, nor by austerity without a true aim. But the wise one who strives by these means enters the home of Brahman.
up_mundaka.3.2.4.sa: नायमात्मा बलहीनेन लभ्यो न च प्रमादात् तपसो वाप्यलिङ्गात् । एतैरुपायैर्यतते यस्तु विद्वांस्तस्यैष आत्मा विशते ब्रह्मधाम ॥

up_mundaka.3.2.8.m: As flowing rivers disappear into the sea, giving up name and form, so the knower, freed from name and form, goes to the divine person beyond the beyond.
roles: Shows the knower's identity as the sea, not the river's name.
up_mundaka.3.2.8.sa: यथा नद्यः स्यन्दमानाः समुद्रेऽस्तं गच्छन्ति नामरूपे विहाय । तथा विद्वान् नामरूपाद्विमुक्तः परात्परं पुरुषमुपैति दिव्यम् ॥

up_narayana.16.m: Peaceful in form, resting on the serpent, lotus-naveled, lord of the gods, support of the universe, vast as the sky, cloud-coloured, beautiful; beloved of Lakshmi, lotus-eyed, reached by yogis in meditation: I bow to Vishnu, who takes away the fear of worldly life, the one lord of all worlds.
roles: The first word is peaceful in form and the verse is a picture to rest the mind on.
up_narayana.16.sa: शान्ताकारं भुजगशयनं पद्मनाभं सुरेशं विश्वाधारं गगनसदृशं मेघवर्णं शुभाङ्गम् । लक्ष्मीकान्तं कमलनयनं योगिभिर्ध्यानगम्यं वन्दे विष्णुं भवभयहरं सर्वलोकैकनाथम् ॥

up_niralamb.13.m: And what is caste? It is not of the skin, nor of the blood, nor of the flesh, nor of the bones. The self has no caste; caste is a convention made for worldly dealings.
roles: Shows one's standing resting on the self which has no rank.
up_niralamb.13.sa: जातिरिति च न चर्मणो न रक्तस्य न मांसस्य न चास्थिनः । न जातिरात्मनो जातिर्व्यवहारप्रकल्पिता ।

up_niralamb.21.m: What is heaven? The company of the good is heaven. What is hell? Contact with the false world and with people lost in its objects is hell.
roles: Choose company as one would choose a world to live in.
up_niralamb.21.sa: स्वर्ग इति च सत्संसर्गः स्वर्गः । नरक इति च असत्संसारविषयजनसंसर्ग एव नरकः ॥

up_prashn.19.m: That stainless world of Brahman belongs to those in whom there is no crookedness, no falsehood and no deceit.
roles: Shows integrity as one's whole qualification.
up_prashn.19.sa: तेषामसौ विरजो ब्रह्मलोको न येषु जिह्ममनृतं न माया चेति ॥

up_prashn.23.m: Out of pride, breath seemed to rise to leave the body, and as it rose all the others had to rise; as it settled, they all settled. As bees all fly out when their queen flies out and settle when she settles, so did speech, mind, eye and ear. Pleased, they praised breath.
roles: The senses that boasted find they cannot even stay without the breath.
up_prashn.23.sa: सोऽभिमानादूर्ध्वमुत्क्रामत इव तस्मिन्नुत्क्रामत्यथेतरे सर्व एवोत्क्रामन्ते तस्मिंश्च प्रतिष्ठमाने सर्व एव प्रतिष्ठन्ते । तद्यथा मक्षिका मधुकरराजानमुत्क्रामन्तं सर्व एवोत्क्रमन्ते तस्मिंष्च प्रतिष्ठमाने सर्व एव प्रातिष्टन्त एवं वाङ्मनष्चक्षुः श्रोत्रं च ते प्रीताः प्राणं स्तुन्वन्ति ॥

scene.s: The senses boast that they keep the body going; breath decides to show them.

up_prashn.3.m: The sage said to them: 'Live here one more year with discipline, self-restraint and faith. Then ask whatever you wish. If we know, we will tell you all of it.'
roles: A year of preparation before the question.
up_prashn.3.sa: तान्ह स ऋषिरुवाच भूय एव तपसा ब्रह्मचर्येण श्रद्धया संवत्सरं संवत्स्यथ यथाकामं प्रश्नान् पृच्छत यदि विज्ञास्यामः सर्वं ह वो वक्ष्याम इति ॥

scene.s: Six earnest seekers come to the sage Pippalada with questions. Instead of answering, he asks them to live with him for a year in discipline and faith, and only promises to answer what he actually knows.

up_prashn.72.m: Sukesha asked: 'Sir, Hiranyanabha, a prince of Kosala, came and asked me: do you know the person of sixteen parts? I told the boy: I do not know him. If I knew him, why would I not tell you? Whoever speaks untruth dries up to the root; so I cannot tell a lie. He silently mounted his chariot and left. Now I ask you: where is that person?'
roles: He let the prince leave unimpressed and kept his word clean.
up_prashn.72.sa: अथ हैनं सुकेशा भारद्वाजः पप्रच्छ । भगवन् हिरण्यनाभः कौसल्यो राजपुत्रो मामुपेत्यैतं प्रश्नमपृच्छत । षोडशकलं भारद्वाज पुरुषं वेत्थ । तमहं कुमारमब्रुवं नाहमिमं वेद । यद्यहमिममवेदिषं कथं ते नावक्ष्यमिति । समूलो वा एष परिशुष्यति योऽनृतमभिवदति तस्मान्नार्हम्यनृतं वक्तुम् । स तूष्णीं रथमारुह्य प्रवव्राज । तं त्वा पृच्छामि क्वासौ पुरुष इति ॥

scene.s: A prince once asked Sukesha a hard question. Rather than bluff, Sukesha said 'I do not know,' because whoever lies withers to the root. The prince drove off in silence, and Sukesha carried the question to his teacher.

up_shiv_sankalp.1.m: That divine mind which travels far when we are awake and likewise when we sleep, the far-going one light among lights: may that mind of mine be of kind and good resolve.
roles: Shows 'may my mind be of good resolve' as a nightly and morning refrain.
up_shiv_sankalp.1.sa: यज्जाग्र॑तो दू॒रमु॒दैति॒ दैवं॒ तदु॑ सु॒प्तस्य॒ तथै॒वैति॑ । दू॒रं॒ग॒मं ज्योति॑षां॒ ज्योति॒रेकं॒ तन्मे॒ मनः॑ शि॒वसं॑कल्पमस्तु ॥

up_shiv_sankalp.6.m: Like a good charioteer guiding horses with the reins, the mind leads people; set in the heart, ageless and swiftest: may that mind of mine be of kind and good resolve.
roles: The driver of one's life is asked to intend well.
up_shiv_sankalp.6.sa: सु॒षा॒र॒थिरश्वा॑निव॒ यन्म॑नु॒ष्या॒न्नेनी॒यते॒ऽभीशु॑भिर्वा॒जिन॑ इव । हृ॒त्प्रति॑ष्ठं॒ यद॑जि॒रं जवि॑ष्ठं॒ तन्मे॒ मनः॑ शि॒वसं॑कल्पमस्तु ॥

up_shwetashwetar.1.1.m: What is the cause? Is it Brahman? From where are we born? By what do we live? Where do we finally rest? Under whose rule, O knowers of Brahman, do we pass through joys and sorrows?
roles: The oldest questions, asked together and without embarrassment.
up_shwetashwetar.1.1.sa: किं कारणं ब्रह्म कुतः स्म जाता जीवाम केन क्व च सम्प्रतिष्ठा । अधिष्ठिताः केन सुखेतरेषु वर्तामहे ब्रह्मविदो व्यवस्थाम् ॥

up_shwetashwetar.1.15.m: As oil in sesame seeds, butter in curd, water in springs and fire in fire-sticks, so is the self found within oneself by one who seeks it with truth and discipline.
roles: Shows the self hidden in oneself and drawn out.
up_shwetashwetar.1.15.sa: तिलेषु तैलं दधिनीव सर्पिरापः स्रोतःस्वरणीषु चाग्निः । एवमात्माऽत्मनि गृह्यतेऽसौसत्येनैनं तपसायोऽनुपश्यति ॥

up_shwetashwetar.3.17.m: He shines through the powers of all the senses yet has no senses; he is the master and ruler of all, the refuge of all, the friend of all.
roles: Gives a refuge open to all.
up_shwetashwetar.3.17.sa: सर्वेन्द्रियगुणाभासं सर्वेन्द्रियविवर्जितम् । सर्वस्य प्रभुमीशानं सर्वस्य शरणं सुहृत् ॥

up_shwetashwetar.3.20.m: Smaller than the small, greater than the great, the Self is hidden in the heart of every creature. One free of grasping sees him, the Lord in his greatness, by the grace of the Creator, and is free of sorrow.
roles: Names the self hidden in the heart.
up_shwetashwetar.3.20.sa: अणोरणीयान् महतो महीयानात्मा गुहायां निहितोऽस्य जन्तोः । तमक्रतुः पश्यति वीतशोको धातुः प्रसादान्महिमानमीशम् ॥

up_shwetashwetar.3.5.m: Rudra, that form of yours which is kind, not fearsome, shining with goodness: with that most peaceful form, dweller on the mountain, look upon us.
roles: The form invoked is the most peaceful one.
up_shwetashwetar.3.5.sa: या ते रुद्र शिवा तनूरघोराऽपापकाशिनी । तया नस्तनुवा शन्तमया गिरिशन्ताभिचाकशीहि ॥

up_shwetashwetar.4.11.m: He who alone presides over every source, in whom this whole world comes together and dissolves: knowing that Lord, the giver of blessings, the God worthy of praise, one comes to utter peace.
roles: Shows peace tied to knowing who holds the whole.
up_shwetashwetar.4.11.sa: यो योनिं योनिमधितिष्ठत्येको यस्मिन्निदं सं च विचैति सर्वम् । तमीशानं वरदं देवमीड्यं निचाय्येमां शान्तिमत्यन्तमेति ॥

up_shwetashwetar.4.14.m: Subtler than the subtlest, in the midst of chaos, the creator of everything, of many forms, the One who embraces the whole world: knowing him as Shiva, the kind one, one attains peace for ever.
roles: Shows peace that does not wait for the chaos to end.
up_shwetashwetar.4.14.sa: सूक्ष्मातिसूक्ष्मं कलिलस्य मध्ये विश्वस्य स्रष्ठारमनेकरूपम् । विश्वस्यैकं परिवेष्टितारं ज्ञात्वा शिवं शान्तिमत्यन्तमेति ॥

up_shwetashwetar.4.15.m: He is the guardian of the world in time, the lord of all, hidden in every being, in whom sages and gods are united. Knowing him so, one cuts the nooses of death.
roles: Shows death's nooses are cut by knowledge.
up_shwetashwetar.4.15.sa: स एव काले भुवनस्य गोप्ता विश्वाधिपः सर्वभूतेषु गूढः । यस्मिन् युक्ता ब्रह्मर्षयो देवताश्च तमेवं ज्ञात्वा मृत्युपाशांश्छिनत्ति ॥

up_shwetashwetar.4.21.m: Knowing you as the Unborn, someone afraid comes to you for refuge: Rudra, with that kind, southern face of yours, protect me always.
roles: Shows asking for protection is itself the practice.
up_shwetashwetar.4.21.sa: अजात इत्येवं कश्चिद्भीरुः प्रपद्यते । रुद्र यत्ते दक्षिणं मुखं तेन मां पाहि नित्यम् ॥

up_shwetashwetar.4.22.m: Do not harm our little ones or our children, our lives, our cattle or our horses. Rudra, in anger do not strike down our brave ones. Bringing offerings, we call on you always.
up_shwetashwetar.4.22.sa: मा नस्तोके तनये मा न आयुषि मा नो गोषु मा न अश्वेषु रीरिषः । वीरान् मा नो रुद्र भामितो वधीर्हविष्मन्तः सदामित् त्वा हवामहे ॥

up_shwetashwetar.6.11.m: One God is hidden in all beings: all-pervading, the inner self of every being, overseer of all action, dwelling in all beings, the witness, pure awareness, alone, beyond all qualities.
roles: Names the innermost self as the witness, awareness itself.
up_shwetashwetar.6.11.sa: एको देवः सर्वभूतेषु गूढः सर्वव्यापी सर्वभूतान्तरात्मा। कर्माध्यक्षः सर्वभूताधिवासः साक्षी चेता केवलो निर्गुणश्च ॥

up_shwetashwetar.6.18.m: He who first brings forth Brahma and hands him the Vedas: to that God, who lights up the understanding of the self, I, longing for freedom, go for refuge.
roles: Shows inquiry ending in leaning on the one who lights the mind.
up_shwetashwetar.6.18.sa: यो ब्रह्माणं विदधाति पूर्वं यो वै वेदांश्च प्रहिणोति तस्मै । तं ह देवं आत्मबुद्धिप्रकाशं मुमुक्षुर्वै शरणमहं प्रपद्ये ॥

up_skand.1.m: Mahadeva, by a mere trace of your compassion I am unshaken; I am pure knowing; I am Shiva. What could be more than this?
roles: I am a mass of knowing, I am Shiva.
up_skand.1.sa: अच्युतोऽस्मि महादेव तव कारुण्यलेशतः । विज्ञानघन एवास्मि शिवोऽस्मि किमतः परम् ॥

up_taittiriya.103.m: That which is well made is the essence itself. Having found that essence, a person becomes joyful.
roles: Shows joy traced to one source, tasted in every joy.
up_taittiriya.103.sa: यद्वै तत् सुकृतम् रसो वै सः रसꣳह्येवायं लब्ध्वाऽऽनन्दी भवति ।

up_taittiriya.108.m: Now an inquiry into joy. Let there be a young man, good, well read, quick, firm and strong, and let this whole earth full of wealth be his: that is one measure of human joy. A hundred human joys make one joy of the human gandharvas, and so too is the joy of a learned one untouched by desire.
roles: Names joy grows as wanting falls.
up_taittiriya.108.sa: सैषाऽऽनन्दस्य मीमाꣳसा भवति । युवा स्यात्साधुयुवाऽध्यायकः । आशिष्ठो दृढिष्ठो बलिष्ठः । तस्येयं पृथिवी सर्वा वित्तस्य पूर्णा स्यात् । स एको मानुष आनन्दः । ते ये शतं मानुषा आनन्दाः । स एको मनुष्यगन्धर्वाणामानन्दः । श्रोत्रियस्य चाकामहतस्य ।

up_taittiriya.124.m: That from which words turn back, along with the mind, not reaching it: whoever knows the joy of Brahman fears nothing at all.
roles: Gives fearlessness coming from knowing a joy that is one's own.
up_taittiriya.124.sa: यतो वाचो निवर्तन्ते । अप्राप्य मनसा सह । आनन्दं ब्रह्मणो विद्वान्। न बिभेति कुतश्चनेति ।

up_taittiriya.125.m: Such a one is no longer tormented by the thought: why did I not do good? Why did I do wrong?
roles: Shows the knower fears nothing from anywhere.
up_taittiriya.125.sa: एतꣳह वाव न तपति । किमहꣳसाधु नाकरवम् । किमहं पापमकरवमिति ।

up_taittiriya.127.m: Bhrigu, son of Varuna, went to his father and said, 'Sir, teach me Brahman.' He told him: food, breath, eye, ear, mind, speech. Then he said: 'That from which these beings are born, by which they live once born, and into which they enter at death: seek to know that. That is Brahman.' Bhrigu practised disciplined reflection.
roles: Shows Bhrigu going away and working on it.
up_taittiriya.127.sa: भृगुर्वै वारुणिः । वरुणं पितरमुपससार । अधीहि भगवो ब्रह्मेति । तस्मा एतत्प्रोवाच । अन्नं प्राणं चक्षुः श्रोत्रं मनो वाचमिति । तꣳहोवाच । यतो वा इमानि भूतानि जायन्ते । येन जातानि जीवन्ति। यत्प्रयन्त्यभिसंविशन्ति। तद्विजिज्ञासस्व । तद्ब्रह्मेति । स तपोऽतप्यत । स तपस्तप्त्वा ॥

scene.s: Bhrigu asks his father Varuna to teach him what is ultimate. Varuna gives only a clue and tells him to reflect. Bhrigu comes back four times with answers (food, breath, mind, understanding) and each time is sent back to go deeper, until he discovers that everything is born from joy, lives by joy and returns to joy.

up_taittiriya.132.m: 'Sir, teach me Brahman.' He said to him: 'Seek to know Brahman by disciplined reflection. Disciplined reflection is Brahman.'
roles: Each incomplete answer is met with go back and reflect again.
up_taittiriya.132.sa: अधीहि भगवो ब्रह्मेति । तꣳहोवाच । तपसा ब्रह्म विजिज्ञासस्व । तपो ब्रह्मेति ।

scene.s: Bhrigu asks his father Varuna to teach him what is ultimate. Varuna gives only a clue and tells him to reflect. Bhrigu comes back four times with answers (food, breath, mind, understanding) and each time is sent back to go deeper, until he discovers that everything is born from joy, lives by joy and returns to joy.

up_taittiriya.146.m: He understood that joy is Brahman. From joy these beings are born, by joy they live once born, and into joy they enter at death. This is the wisdom of Bhrigu and Varuna, established in the highest space. Whoever knows this becomes established.
roles: Names joy as the source one comes from and lives by.
up_taittiriya.146.sa: आनन्दो ब्रह्मेति व्यजानात्। आनन्दाध्येव खल्विमानि भूतानि जायन्ते । आनन्देन जातानि जीवन्ति । आनन्दं प्रयन्त्यभिसंविशन्तीति । सैषा भार्गवी वारुणी विद्या । परमे व्योमन्प्रतिष्ठिता ।स य एवं वेद प्रतितिष्ठति ।

up_taittiriya.149.m: Do not speak ill of food; that is a vow. Breath is food, the body eats food; the body rests on breath and breath rests in the body.
roles: Shows respect for what keeps the body and breath going, kept as a daily vow.
up_taittiriya.149.sa: अन्नं न निन्द्यात् । तद्व्रतम् । प्राणो वा अन्नम् । शरीरमन्नादम् । प्राणे शरीरं प्रतिष्ठितम् ।

up_taittiriya.158.m: Turn no one away from your home; that is a vow. So one should gather plenty of food by whatever means, for people say of such a person: food is ready for him.
roles: Shows whoever comes for shelter being received.
up_taittiriya.158.sa: सदाचारप्रदर्शनम् । ब्रह्मानन्दानुभवःन कञ्चन वसतौ प्रत्याचक्षीत । तद्व्रतम् । तस्माद्यया कया च विधया बह्वन्नं प्राप्नुयात् ।

up_taittiriya.43.m: Right conduct, along with study and teaching. Truth, along with study and teaching. Discipline, along with study and teaching. Self-control, along with study and teaching.
roles: Learning runs alongside every other duty, never replaced by them.
up_taittiriya.43.sa: ऋतं च स्वाध्यायप्रवचने च। सत्यं च स्वाध्यायप्रवचने च। तपश्च स्वाध्यायप्रवचने च। दमश्च स्वाध्यायप्रवचने च।

up_taittiriya.49.m: Having taught the Veda, the teacher instructs the student: Speak the truth. Practise what is right. Do not neglect your study.
roles: Shows study is to be kept up, not finished.
up_taittiriya.49.sa: वेदमनूच्याचार्योन्तेवासिनमनुशास्ति । सत्यं वद । धर्मं चर । स्वाध्यायान्मा प्रमदः ।

up_taittiriya.50.m: Having brought your teacher the gift he values, do not cut off the line of your family. Do not drift from truth. Do not drift from what is right. Do not neglect your wellbeing. Do not neglect your prosperity. Do not neglect study and teaching.
roles: Shows keeping welfare and prosperity inside a dharmic life.
up_taittiriya.50.sa: आचार्याय प्रियं धनमाहृत्य प्रजातन्तुं मा व्यवच्छेत्सीः । सत्यान्न प्रमदितव्यम् । धर्मान्न प्रमदितव्यम् । कुशलान्न प्रमदितव्यम् । भूत्यै न प्रमदितव्यम् । स्वाध्यायप्रवचनाभ्यां न प्रमदितव्यम् ॥

up_taittiriya.52.m: Do not neglect your duties to the gods and the ancestors. Let your mother be a god to you. Let your father be a god to you. Let your teacher be a god to you. Let your guest be a god to you.
roles: Shows those who raised and taught you are to be honoured as one honours a deity.
up_taittiriya.52.sa: देवपितृकार्याभ्यां न प्रमदितव्यम् । मातृदेवो भव । पितृदेवो भव । आचार्यदेवो भव । अतिथिदेवो भव ।

up_taittiriya.53.m: Whatever actions are blameless, those you should do, and not others. Whatever good conduct is ours, that you should follow.
roles: Shows one's own conscience is given standing.
up_taittiriya.53.sa: यान्यनवद्यानि कर्माणि । तानि सेवितव्यानि । नो इतराणि । यान्यस्माकꣳसुचरितानि । तानि त्वयोपास्यानि ॥

up_taittiriya.54.m: Not the other things. Whoever are better than us, offer them a seat and refreshment. Give with faith; do not give without faith. Give generously. Give with modesty. Give with respect. Give with understanding.
roles: Gives with understanding of the one who receives.
up_taittiriya.54.sa: नो इतराणि । ये के चारुमच्छ्रेयाꣳसो ब्राह्मणाः । तेषां त्वयाऽऽसनेन प्रश्वसितव्यम् । श्रद्धया देयम् । अश्रद्धयाऽदेयम् । श्रिया देयम् । ह्रिया देयम् । भिया देयम् । संविदा देयम् ।

up_taittiriya.56.m: Now, if you are ever unsure about an action or about conduct, look to the thoughtful people there: devoted, independent, not harsh, lovers of what is right. As they would act, so should you act. And towards people under accusation, act as such people would. This is the instruction, this is the teaching.
roles: Shows judgement borrowed from thoughtful unforced unharsh people.
up_taittiriya.56.sa: अथ यदि ते कर्मविचिकित्सा वा वृत्तविचिकित्सा वा स्यात् ॥ ये तत्र ब्राह्मणाः संमर्शिनः । युक्ता आयुक्ताः । अलूक्षा धर्मकामाः स्युः । यथा ते तत्र वर्तेरन् । तथा तत्र वर्तेथाः । अथाभ्याख्यातेषु । ये तत्र ब्राह्मणाः संमर्शिनः । युक्ता आयुक्ताः । अलूक्षा धर्मकामाः स्युः । यथा ते तेषु वर्तेरन् । तथा तेषु वर्तेथाः । एष आदेशः । एष उपदेशः ।
